b_rows_sample.statement: Document-wide status discipline: everything in this conceptual foundation document is Candidate/Hypothesis input to a future P4 Constitutional Invariant Map; nothing is adopted or SHALL; the existing EKS baseline (the 'f0106657' precedent) is untouched.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Human ↔ Governance ↔ KnowledgeOS ↔ Agent ↔ Engineering ↔ Runtime
a_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 125 (KnowledgeOS Operating Model), stating the principal-actor chain Human<->Governance<->KnowledgeOS<->Agent<->Engineering<->Runtime and posing the question 'who does what, who is allowed to decide what, and where does evidence flow?' across Domain Architect, Architecture Board, engineers, deterministic assurance, KnowledgeOS, Claude, Codex, and runtime systems.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Business/Product Authority, Domain Architect, Architecture Board/Governance, Engineering Team, Deterministic Assurance, AI Agent, Runtime/Operational Systems
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies seven principal actor classes and states KnowledgeOS itself is not an organizational actor but 'the system of record and coordination substrate through which these actors exchange governed knowledge and evidence.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: BusinessIntent ... Why are we doing this?
a_rows_sample.statement: Assigns responsibilities per actor: Business/Product Authority establishes BusinessIntent (objectives, regulatory/customer requirements, strategic priorities, risk acceptance) answering 'why,' without determining technical architecture; Domain Architect translates business/technical concerns into architectural reasoning (analysis, bounded-context decisions, principles, alternatives, impact analysis, recommendations, governance prep) under ArchitecturalRecommendation ≠ GovernanceDecision; Architecture Board consumes Evidence+Recommendation+Impact+Alternatives to produce Analysis->BoardDecision rather than performing every technical analysis itself; Engineering transforms authorized intent into implementation (Decision->Implementation) owning code/config/deployment/tests/technical remediation/operational changes within delegation; Deterministic Assurance answers machine-testable conformance questions (Assurance->Evidence, not Assurance->OrganizationalAuthority); AI Agent participates in retrieval/analysis/reasoning/inspection/tool execution/checks/recommendations/delegated execution but Agent ≠ GovernanceAuthority; Runtime/Operations is the source of observed reality answering 'what is actually happening'; KnowledgeOS holds Knowledge+Evidence+Provenance+Authority+TemporalValidity+Traceability+Feedback as the semantic continuity layer between decisions and reality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Responsible ... Authorized.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Responsible from Authorized (an engineer can be responsible for implementing a decision without authority to change it; an architect can recommend without authority to approve; an agent can execute a delegated action without authority to redefine policy), and argues a conventional RACI matrix is insufficient — KnowledgeOS needs Actor+Capability+Authority+Scope+EvidenceResponsibility.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Authority = Actor × Action × Resource × Scope × Validity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Authority = Actor x Action x Resource x Scope x Validity (e.g. Engineering Team/deploy/Service X/Staging/current may be authorized while the same tuple in production may require different authority); for agents, AgentAuthority = DelegatedAuthority ∩ Policy, so an agent cannot inherit all authority of the human whose credentials it uses — e.g. being authorized to 'run tests and create a PR' gives AgentCapability={read,test,createPR} which does not imply merge or deployProduction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | Actor | Primary responsibility | Can recommend? | Can decide? | Can execute? | Produces evidence? |
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents a first-approximation operating-model matrix (Business Authority, Domain Architect, Architecture Board, Engineering, Assurance, AI Agent, Runtime rows) recording each actor's recommend/decide/execute/evidence capacities, explicitly labeled a working model, not yet a finalized organizational RACI.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Business Intent → Architecture → Governance Decision → Engineering → Runtime → Observation → Evidence → KnowledgeOS → Governance
a_rows_sample.statement: Diagrams the evidence-flow loop, and separately the decision-flow Question->Analysis->Recommendation->Decision->Authorization->Action (agent participates heavily in the first three, authority governs the fourth/fifth, engineering executes the sixth); warns evidence flow and decision flow must not be confused — Evidence->Recommendation is possible, but Evidence->Decision is not automatically valid without an intervening governance mechanism.

a_rows_sample.anchor: GovernanceDecision → Knowledge → AgentContext → EngineeringAction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the bottom-up half (Runtime->Observation->Evidence->Finding->GovernanceInput) and the reverse top-down half (GovernanceDecision->Knowledge->AgentContext->EngineeringAction), together making KnowledgeOS the semantic bridge Governance <-> EngineeringReality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Architect = Classification/Assessment; GovernancePolicy = DefinesDecisionAuthority.
a_rows_sample.statement: Answers 'is the Domain Architect the person who decides whether something requires governance?' — generally no: the architect performs Classification/Assessment while GovernancePolicy defines decision authority; the architect may apply governance rules but should not be sole authority source unless explicitly assigned; worked with a Nexus-upgrade example flow (change -> engineering/project -> business+architecture assessment -> governance classification -> required path -> decision -> implementation) where authority belongs to the organizational governance framework, not automatically to whoever performed the assessment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: BusinessImpact, ArchitectureImpact, SecurityImpact, OperationalImpact, RegulatoryImpact, TechnologyRisk.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes governance should be triggered by change characteristics, not personal judgment alone, listing six trigger dimensions; defines a classification engine Change->Classification with results Standard/Governed/ArchitectureRelevant/SecurityRelevant/HighRisk, automatable for simple cases but policy-defined in meaning; an agent may gather affected components/dependencies/decisions/runtime impact/historical changes/similar cases and recommend a classification, but Recommendation ≠ FinalClassification unless delegated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance Package ├── Change ... └── Recommendation
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a Governance Package KnowledgeOS should assemble (Change, Business Intent, Affected Systems, Architecture Context, Existing Decisions, Runtime Evidence, Security Evidence, Risk, Agent Analysis, Deterministic Checks, Recommendation) so the human decision-maker receives a decision-ready evidence package rather than a pile of documents — framed as where KnowledgeOS provides real value, an 'engineering decision-support system' able to answer what changed/expected/deployed/governing-decisions/evidence/risks/governance-path/agent-conclusion/checks-passed/remaining-uncertainty.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Task → RelevantContext.
a_rows_sample.statement: States agent context construction should be task-scoped (Task->RelevantContext = AuthoritativeKnowledge+RelevantEvidence+CurrentState+ApplicablePolicy) rather than the entire knowledge universe; every context element should retain SourceID so the agent can cite provenance ('this comes from ADR-042, effective since June 2026') rather than an unattributed 'the system told me this.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Constitutional rules ... 9. Historical context
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a nine-level context precedence hierarchy (constitutional rules, applicable governance policies, current authoritative decisions, current architecture, verified implementation state, runtime observations, approved exceptions, agent inference, historical context), noting actual precedence must be formally defined rather than assumed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rule + Exception → EffectiveState.
a_rows_sample.statement: Models exception handling as Rule+Exception->EffectiveState rather than the exception destroying the rule (e.g. Rule: UseArchitectureA; Exception: ServiceX may use B until T; Effective(ServiceX,t<T)=B while Effective(OtherService,t)=A); requires an agent to retrieve both Rule and ApplicableExceptions since ignoring an exception creates false findings — Conformance = ExpectedRule + ExceptionContext.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Business → Domain Architect → Architecture Board → KnowledgeOS → {Claude, Codex} → Engineering → Runtime → Evidence → KnowledgeOS
a_rows_sample.statement: Diagrams the complete, deliberately circular actor-interaction chain and states KnowledgeOS is 'the continuity layer' preventing the fragmentation that would otherwise occur when BusinessDecision, Architecture, Code, Runtime, Evidence, and AgentContext each live in separate, disconnected systems.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Agents can participate in governance workflows; they do not automatically possess governance authority.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 125 verdict: the operating model Business->Architecture->Governance->KnowledgeOS->Agent->Engineering->Runtime->Evidence->KnowledgeOS with explicit Knowledge/Classification/Authorization/Assurance/Closure gates, and the central organizational principle that agents can participate in governance workflows without automatically possessing governance authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Human{Developer,Domain Architect,Architecture Board,Governance,Operations} → KnowledgeOS{AI Agents,Assurance,Governance,Engineering Systems}. Who does what, who owns the resulting knowledge, who can decide, and what evidence must exist before the next step is allowed?
b_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 156 (KnowledgeOS Operating Model): shifts from a primarily technical artifact to defining how humans, AI agents, governance bodies, and engineering systems interact day-to-day, connecting directly to the Domain Architect/Architecture Board/Softwareeinführungsprozess/IT Change Management governance work developed elsewhere.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge → Context → Inquiry → Decision → Action → Observation → Evidence → Assurance → Learning, under Governance. Governance → Knowledge → Engineering → Evidence → Governance.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the fundamental operating equation and the primary organizational feedback loop, reframing Step 156 from 'who uses KnowledgeOS' to how governed knowledge moves through the organization while preserving authority, provenance, accountability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Human{Developer,Domain Architect,Architecture Board/Governance,Operations}, AI{Engineering/Architecture/Analysis/Assurance-support agents}, System{repositories,CI/CD,runtime,monitoring,infrastructure,external systems}. Actor ≠ Authority. AI Agent ≠ Governance Authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines five operating actor categories across Human/AI/System, rejecting a simple 'users vs system' model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Know (what is believed/declared true?), Decide (what should be permitted/required?), Act (what should be changed?), Assure (did reality conform?). Know→Decide→Act→Assure, with evidence flowing back into knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines four responsibility classes and the KnowledgeOS responsibility triangle (Authority decides at the apex, Knowledge<->Action on one axis, Assurance verifying below).

b_rows_sample.anchor: AI may reason, humans remain accountable (unless explicitly delegated) — an authority-boundary principle, not an anti-AI principle.
b_rows_sample.statement: States human accountability for authority-requiring decisions; defines the AI operating role as Observe/Understand/Retrieve/Reason/Propose/Execute-where-authorized/Report, explicitly not Invent authority/Change governance/Rewrite authoritative knowledge/Hide uncertainty/Declare itself correct, formalized as AI Capability ⊆ AuthorizedActionSpace.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agent = Role + Context + Authority + Constraints + Capabilities + EvidenceRequirements. AgentContext{Identity,Role,Task,Knowledge,Provenance,Applicable Rules,Authority,Constraints,Available Tools,Allowed Actions,Evidence Requirements,Verification Requirements}. An agent should never receive only prompt+tools.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the agent operating contract as an important refinement of agent architecture; worked example — 'upgrade Nexus' is not yet a valid action until KnowledgeOS resolves which Nexus/environment/version/approved target/applicable architecture/change process/authorizer/evidence requirement/rollback requirement, connecting directly to the Nexus governance work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1.Observe 2.Ask/Inquire 3.Retrieve Context 4.Establish Applicable Knowledge 5.Analyze 6.Decide 7.Authorize 8.Act 9.Observe Result 10.Produce Evidence 11.Verify 12.Update Knowledge — not every operation requires every stage explicitly, but the semantics must remain available.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the twelve-step operating lifecycle, elaborated per step: Observe produces an Observation, not a conclusion (examples: repository changed, infrastructure changed, proposal created, security finding, Nexus upgrade requested, production incident); Inquiry schema (subject,question,context,requester,purpose,scope); Retrieve Context resolves governed representations (current architecture, Softwareeinführungsprozess, IT Change Management, Nexus architecture, existing ADRs, infrastructure facts, previous decisions, applicable exceptions) rather than reconstructing from arbitrary documents; Establish Applicable Knowledge formalizes ApplicableKnowledge(t,scope,authority) — correct version/effective period/scope/authority/exceptions; Analyze produces an Analysis, not a Decision (worked Nexus-version-vs-target example with impact areas); Decide branches into AUTOMATIC/AUTHORIZED HUMAN/GOVERNANCE paths depending on risk/architecture-relevance/exception status, connecting to the Softwareeinführungsprozess/Change Management/Architecture Board discussion; Authorization remains separate from Decision (Approval ≠ ExecutionPermission, e.g. Board approves target architecture while Developer is authorized to implement it); Action carries ActionId/Actor/AuthorityContext/Target/Intent/Authorization/Timestamp/ExpectedEffect/EvidenceRequirements ('the operational form of the Action Kernel'); Observe Result records raw facts (not yet assurance conclusions); Evidence packages Observation+Source+Method+Timestamp+Context from sources like CI/CD, repository, runtime, infrastructure, test, static analysis, human review, agent analysis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionClass: TECHNICAL, OPERATIONAL, ARCHITECTURAL, GOVERNANCE, EXCEPTION — not every decision has the same authority requirement.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a decision classification taxonomy, exact organizational mapping left to governance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ExpectedArchitecture =? ObservedArchitecture, or Rule(x)=true? Result: PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE/NOT_APPLICABLE. No proof ≠ Proof of violation — INCONCLUSIVE must not silently become FAIL.
b_rows_sample.statement: Strongly retains the INCONCLUSIVE assurance verdict as epistemically distinct from FAIL, with an explicit statistical argument (P(violation|E) may be uncertain, but insufficient evidence must not be treated as proof of violation) — 'one of the strongest statistician-oriented safeguards in KnowledgeOS.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Raw Observation → Evidence → Analysis → Candidate Knowledge → Review → Governance → Authoritative Knowledge. L0 Raw Observation .. L5 Governed/Authoritative Knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the knowledge-promotion pipeline (Update Knowledge stage produces a KnowledgeCandidate, only the governance process elevates it to AuthoritativeKnowledge) and proposes a generic six-level epistemic-authority ladder L0-L5, names not necessarily final but the distinction architecturally valuable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Confidence=0.98 but Authority=0. Confidence ≠ Authority. 500 agents repeating the same statement does not create authority — Authority(frequency) ≠ Authority(source).
b_rows_sample.statement: States two crucial invariants: confidence must never be confused with authority, and popularity/repetition must never be confused with truth/authority — 'precisely why provenance must be structural.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Source→Claim→Interpretation→Decision→Action→Observation→Evidence→Verification, plus Claim{derivedFrom,supportedBy,contextualizedBy,approvedBy,supersedes,contradictedBy}. CONTRADICTION_DETECTED as a first-class concept.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the operating knowledge-graph relationship model, and worked contradiction example (Rule R requires A, Observation shows A absent, another document says A is optional) — KnowledgeOS must not silently pick one but expose CONTRADICTION_DETECTED and route it through Contradiction->Inquiry->Evidence->Authority Resolution->Decision->Knowledge Update, 'exactly what a Knowledge Operating System should do.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Governance resolves which rule applies, which version is authoritative, who may decide, whether this is an exception, which interpretation is valid, when a new rule becomes effective — not merely 'approve documents.'
b_rows_sample.statement: Redefines Governance as a knowledge-resolution mechanism, more precise than 'document approval.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Domain Architect: knowledge and architecture boundary manager (interprets/models/questions/analyzes/proposes/reviews/governs/assures) depending on delegated authority, never silently becoming the source of organizational truth. Architecture Board: Architectural Authority evaluating Proposal/Context/Impact/Evidence/Risk/Principles/Existing Decisions to create GovernanceDecision. Developer: consumes governed context ('what architecture applies to this implementation?'). AI agent: a knowledge-mediated engineering actor (Governed Context+Reasoning+Authorized Capabilities+Evidence Production, not merely LLM+Tools). System actor: provides observational authority over its own state (Git: commit exists; CI: test executed; Runtime: container running; Nexus: repository exists) but not governance authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Assigns operating roles per actor type, restating ObservationAuthority ≠ GovernanceAuthority for system actors.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic Authority (what is authoritative knowledge?), Governance Authority (what is approved?), Execution Authority (who may perform an action?), Observational Authority (what system can establish a fact?).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a four-way authority decomposition proposed to become part of the KnowledgeOS constitutional model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: GOVERNANCE -authoritative knowledge-> KNOWLEDGE -context-> INQUIRY -analysis-> DECISION -authorization-> ACTION -execution-> OBSERVATION -evidence-> ASSURANCE -findings/proof-> GOVERNANCE.
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents the mature complete operating-loop diagram, and combines the previously separate Engineering and Governance Golden Traces into one 'KnowledgeOS Operating Golden Trace': Knowledge->Context->Inquiry->Decision->Authorization->Action->Observation->Evidence->Verification->Knowledge.

Gives a control-theory mathematical interpretation of the operating loop, a feedback-control system with organizational state S_t, action A_t, measurement method M_t, and applicable rule set R_t, described as a 'genuine feedback-control interpretation of KnowledgeOS.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Classical control: error→controller→automatic correction. KnowledgeOS: error→finding→decision→authorized correction. Assurance detects; Governance decides; Authorization permits; Engineering acts.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the crucial constraint distinguishing KnowledgeOS from an automatic controller — this four-part separation 'should become constitutional'; worked failure-handling example (Finding->Classification->Impact->Decision with outcomes FIX/ACCEPT RISK/APPROVE EXCEPTION/REJECT CHANGE/ROLLBACK/INVESTIGATE, the Assurance Engine not choosing among these without delegated authority) contrasting 'AI sees violation->AI changes code' (unsafe) with 'AI sees violation->Finding->Context->Decision authority->Authorized action' (KnowledgeOS's safer path), preventing 'AI governance by accident.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: No system observation, AI inference or engineering action automatically acquires governance authority merely by occurring.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes this single sentence as a constitutional statement protecting the architecture from a large class of future failures.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS remembers what was known, why it was believed, where it came from, who had authority, what decision was made, what action followed, what actually happened, what evidence was produced, whether it conformed, what was learned — substantially more powerful than a knowledge base. KnowledgeOS = Organizational Epistemic Infrastructure.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes KnowledgeOS as organizational memory and then as 'Organizational Epistemic Infrastructure' — concerned with how the organization establishes, preserves, contextualizes and validates what it treats as knowledge, explicitly framed as the destination the Chapter 4 validation pointed toward.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'kos-operating-model-step156-preview' POSSIBLY relates to 'knowledgeos-operating-model' (batch B0025). Note: Step 156's opening framing (following the Step 155 Governance Runtime): a human/AI/governance/engineering day-to-day interaction model, distinct from but continuing the earlier S1024 knowledgeos-operating-model (Step 125).

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Theory is the formal theory ... to answer: How can a system represent, transform, evaluate, preserve, revise, and act upon knowledge without confusing reality, information, evidence, truth, determination, decision, and action? It is not yet a finished universal 'Knowledge Algebra.' The strongest current form is a theory of epistemic state, representation, evidence, inquiry, propositions, and transformations, with some parts still explicitly research-stage.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the central question KnowledgeOS Theory answers and its current honest scope: a theory of epistemic state/representation/evidence/inquiry/propositions/transformations, explicitly not yet a finished universal Knowledge Algebra.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reality -> Observation -> Information -> Representation -> Proposition -> Evidence -> Warrant/Reasoning -> KnowledgeState -> Determination -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action -> Outcome -> NewEvidence. Evidence is not Truth. Observation is not Evidence. Representation is not Ontology. Determination is not Truth unless a soundness bridge has been established. Decision is not Determination. Decision is not Action. Unknown is not False. Correlation is not Causation. A graph is not automatically a Knowledge State. A path is not automatically an inference. Hash equality is not semantic identity. These distinctions prevent the system from making epistemic category errors.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the fourteen-stage conceptual chain from Reality to NewEvidence and eleven protective non-identities (Evidence!=Truth, Observation!=Evidence, Representation!=Ontology, Determination!=Truth without a soundness bridge, Decision!=Determination, Decision!=Action, Unknown!=False, Correlation!=Causation, graph!=KnowledgeState, path!=inference, hash-equality!=semantic-identity), framed as preventing epistemic category errors.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = (Content,Support,Uncertainty,Model,Alternatives,History,Identity,Context,Inquiry,Status), but this is currently treated as a semantic decomposition, not necessarily a mandatory implementation tuple. Knowledge State != Representation. Different representations may potentially represent the same semantic state. But the theory is deliberately cautious: semantic equivalence of arbitrary representations has not been universally established.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the K_t semantic decomposition (explicitly non-mandatory) and the Knowledge State != Representation principle, cautioning that semantic equivalence of arbitrary representations is not universally established -- directly consistent with this same batch's F4 audit findings on equiv_sem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [[s]]_Gamma = p where s is a representation/sentence and p is the proposition interpreted under context Gamma. Truth(p,w,Gamma,t) in {0,1}. This allows the theory to distinguish assertion != determination != truth.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the proposition-interpretation formalization [[s]]_Gamma=p and truth evaluation Truth(p,w,Gamma,t), supporting the three-way distinction assertion != determination != truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ev(e,p,Gamma,t) meaning that evidence e bears upon proposition p under context Gamma at time t. Evidence != Truth and Evidence != Knowledge. two pieces of evidence != two independent pieces of evidence. Two documents may simply copy the same original source. path != independent evidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates evidence as a relational predicate Ev(e,p,Gamma,t) rather than a property of an object, deriving Evidence!=Truth, Evidence!=Knowledge, and the independence warning that multiple evidence items copying the same source do not constitute independent corroboration, nor does a mere graph path constitute independent evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: q=<X,Y,Gamma,tau,Pi,Lambda> and more fundamentally an inquiry can be understood as an answer-producing function q:W->Y. This leads to the concept of inquiry-relative adequacy. A representation does not have to preserve everything. It has to preserve what is necessary to answer the inquiry correctly.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the inquiry formalization as a six-tuple and as an answer-producing function q:W->Y, grounding the concept of inquiry-relative adequacy (a representation need only preserve what answers the inquiry correctly, not everything).

a_rows_sample.anchor: T:X->X' transforms a representation. Q=g o T where Q is the inquiry-relevant observable. The preservation condition can be expressed as Pi o T = Pi o T o E_S for an appropriate elimination/reduction structure. This provides the foundation for reasoning about reduction, elimination, equivalence, sufficient representations, preservation, semantic invariants, and Zero.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the transformation and preservation formalization (T:X->X', Q=g∘T, the preservation condition Pi∘T=Pi∘T∘E_S), naming it the foundation for the whole reduction/elimination/equivalence/Zero research family already covered extensively in this batch's kr-rep-reduction-related documents.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is not simply the number 0. A Knowledge Gap can be represented as a set of unsatisfied requirements: Delta_t = {r in R_t: not Sat(K_t,r)}. Then Delta_t=empty means that there is no remaining requirement gap under the relevant satisfaction semantics. Zero equiv empty gap rather than merely numerical zero. This connects your algebraic work with the epistemic theory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates Zero as structurally equivalent to an empty requirement gap (Delta_t=empty) rather than numerical zero, explicitly connecting the algebraic Zero research line to the epistemic Delta_t/Sat theory just extensively audited in this same batch.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1} = T(K_t,E_{t+1},Q_t,C_t,EC_t,A_t). H_{t+1}=H_t union {transition_t}. current candidate operation nucleus includes ASSERT, LINK, REVISE, RETRACT, ISOLATE. But importantly, these are not all canonically frozen as the final minimal operation set. Operation minimality remains an open research problem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the state-evolution transition formula and history-append formula, listing a five-operation candidate nucleus (ASSERT/LINK/REVISE/RETRACT/ISOLATE) while explicitly flagging operation minimality as an open research problem, not a frozen final set.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS does not adopt the simplistic rule P, not-P => everything. Instead, contradiction is represented and isolated. real knowledge systems routinely contain conflicting observations, competing hypotheses, outdated information, incompatible sources, different contextual truths. So contradiction is an epistemic state to manage, not a reason to destroy the entire knowledge state.
a_rows_sample.statement: States KnowledgeOS's explicit rejection of classical explosion (P, not-P => everything) in favor of representing and isolating contradiction as a manageable epistemic state, motivated by five named real-world sources of conflicting information.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Status table (15 rows): K_t as epistemic state RESOLVED/RATIFIED; Reality!=knowledge state ESTABLISHED; Evidence!=truth ESTABLISHED; Truth!=determination!=decision ADOPTED/FOUNDATIONAL; Contradiction/non-explosion RESOLVED/ADOPTED; Representation theory SUBSTANTIALLY DEVELOPED; Inquiry semantics DEVELOPED; Proposition semantics DEVELOPED; Evidence semantics DEVELOPED; Transformation theory SUBSTANTIALLY DEVELOPED; Universal Knowledge Algebra NOT ESTABLISHED; Canonical minimal operations OPEN RESEARCH; Complete F4 Sat(K_t,r) semantics NOT ESTABLISHED; Universal semantic equivalence r1 equiv_sem r2 NOT ESTABLISHED; F3<->F4 semantic bridge OPEN.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a comprehensive fifteen-item status table for the whole theory, distinguishing resolved/established/adopted foundations from explicitly open items (universal Knowledge Algebra, canonical minimal operations, complete F4 Sat semantics, universal equiv_sem, F3<->F4 bridge), the last three matching exactly the open items just extensively audited in this same batch's F4/Model-B series.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The existence and role of Sat are present in the historical corpus, but a fully operational, corpus-native definition of Sat(K_t,r) has not yet been recovered. The later Sat* construction is therefore a candidate construction, not proof that the corpus already contained that exact semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Directly cross-references and restates the same-day F4/Model-B audit series' central finding (S2888-S2897): Sat's existence/role are corpus-present but its full operational semantics are not recovered, and Sat* remains a candidate construction rather than recovered corpus semantics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not design what the corpus has not established. Where the corpus is insufficient, the correct result is NOT ESTABLISHED / RESEARCH REQUIRED, not an invented definition.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the closing methodological rule underlying the whole KnowledgeOS research programme: never design what the corpus has not established; an insufficient corpus should yield the honest classification NOT ESTABLISHED/RESEARCH REQUIRED rather than an invented definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Delta_t = {r in R_t | Sat(K_t,r)=0}. Therefore Delta_t=empty is the KnowledgeOS notion of Zero Gap. Zero means that there are no unsatisfied requirements remaining within the defined requirement set and satisfaction semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the core Zero-Gap definition as Delta_t=empty over the requirement set R_t and satisfaction predicate Sat(K_t,r), consistent with the F4/Model-B and kr-rep-reduction lines already covered in this batch.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 0 != empty in general. Numerical zero means a quantity has value zero. KnowledgeOS Zero is closer to: empty residual requirement set.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes numerical zero from KnowledgeOS Zero (an empty residual requirement set), a set-theoretic rather than quantitative notion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is always relative to the defined requirement/inquiry scope. ... Zero Gap != Complete Knowledge. It means only: There is no remaining gap with respect to the requirements currently being evaluated.
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns against conflating Zero Gap with Complete Knowledge or Complete Reality: satisfying all requirements in a scoped requirement set says nothing about knowledge outside that scope.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the same K_t can be Zero relative to R_t while simultaneously being Non-zero relative to a larger R'_t. This makes Zero inquiry- and contract-relative, rather than absolute.
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example showing the identical knowledge state K_t can simultaneously be Zero (empty gap) relative to a smaller requirement set and non-Zero relative to a larger superset, establishing Zero as inherently inquiry- and contract-relative rather than an absolute property of K_t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If a transformation T removes irrelevant information while preserving everything needed to answer the inquiry, then the resulting representation may still have the same gap: Delta(T(K_t))=Delta(K_t). If the gap was already empty, then a valid inquiry-preserving transformation can maintain Delta(T(K_t))=empty. So Zero can function as a preserved semantic condition, not merely as a terminal numerical value.
a_rows_sample.statement: Connects Zero to the transformation/preservation theory: an inquiry-preserving transformation T maintains the gap Delta(T(K_t))=Delta(K_t), so an already-empty gap remains empty under valid transformations, framing Zero as a preserved semantic condition across the reduction/elimination research family.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero_{R,C}(K_t) iff Delta_{R,C}(K_t)=empty, where the subscript reminds us that Zero depends on the relevant requirements R and contract/context C. This is much stronger and safer than saying 'Zero means absence.' It means: There is no unresolved requirement in the specified epistemic task.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the strongest current formulation Zero_{R,C}(K_t) iff Delta_{R,C}(K_t)=empty, explicitly parameterized by requirements R and contract/context C, as a safer and stronger statement than an unparameterized 'Zero means absence.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: the full operational semantics of Sat(K_t,r) is not yet completely established, especially in the historical F4/Model-B work we just discussed. Therefore Delta_t=empty is theoretically meaningful, but we cannot yet claim that every real KnowledgeOS implementation can compute Zero correctly. Zero definition != Zero computation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Self-applies the same day's F4/Model-B audit finding (Sat(K_t,r)'s operational semantics not yet established) to the Zero-Gap concept itself, distinguishing Zero definition (theoretically meaningful) from Zero computation (not currently guaranteed correct in any real implementation).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reality ≠ Observation ≠ Information ≠ Evidence ≠ Knowledge ≠ Decision ≠ Action.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A1 (Semantic Separation) opens Part I of the v2.0 rewrite: reality, observation, information, evidence and knowledge are held to occupy different semantic roles unless a formal equivalence is explicitly established, giving the epistemic lifecycle Reality->Observation->Information->Knowledge->Gap->Inquiry->Determination->Decision->Action->New Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If there exist ω1,ω2 ∈ Ω such that ω1≠ω2 and ρ(ω1)=ρ(ω2), then ρ is not injective and therefore cannot uniquely identify the underlying state of reality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposition 3.1 with proof: an observation map rho:Omega->I need not be injective, so KnowledgeOS must never silently infer Observed(x)=>Reality(x).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Adequate(R,Q,Γ) ⟺ 𝓡_req(Q,Γ) ⊆ Dist(R)
b_rows_sample.statement: The Representation Adequacy Principle: a representation is adequate only if it preserves the distinctions required to answer the declared inquiry under context Gamma, avoiding the impossible requirement of preserving every conceivable distinction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose there exist x1,x2 ∈ X such that x1≠x2 but π(x1)=π(x2). Then any question Q whose required distinction includes x1≠x2 cannot, in general, be answered correctly from π(x) alone.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 16.1 (Loss of Required Distinction), with proof by the impossibility of a deterministic function distinguishing two values a projection maps identically; establishes that a system can be perfectly internally consistent and still epistemically inadequate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Δ_t = {r ∈ Req_t : ¬Sat(K_t,r)} ... Gap = Unsatisfied Requirements.
b_rows_sample.statement: Redefines the Knowledge Gap as a set-theoretic construction (unsatisfied requirements under the current epistemic contract) rather than a subtraction Delta=IdealKnowledge-Knowledge, explicitly rejecting the latter as generally undefined because the two objects need not belong to a common algebraic space.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K_t,EC_t) ⟺ Δ_t = ∅ ... Therefore Zero is contract-relative.
b_rows_sample.statement: Definition 23.1 (Epistemic Zero): Zero means no requirement of the declared epistemic contract remains unsatisfied; explicitly not K_t=Reality and not 'all possible knowledge is known.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Δ_{t+1} ⊆ Δ_t ... every requirement satisfied at t remains satisfied at t+1 ... This theorem depends on the contract remaining fixed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorems 24.1 (Zero Equivalence) and 25.1 (Gap Reduction) are proved, with an explicit limitation that gap comparison across differing contracts (EC_t != EC_{t+1}) requires an explicit compatibility mapping — 'moving the goalposts' is formally blocked by the Contract Compatibility principle GapComparison=>ContractCompatibility.

b_rows_sample.anchor: V(K_t) ⊆ V(K_{t+1}) ∧ H(K_t) ⊆ H(K_{t+1}) ... Historical existence ≠ Current epistemic standing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A6 (Historical Preservation) plus the constitutional distinction between historical existence and current epistemic standing: a proposition can move Supported->Retracted without deleting the historical fact that it was once asserted and supported; replaces 'universal epistemic monotonicity' with this weaker, correct invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth ≠ Evaluation ≠ Determination ≠ Decision.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A2 (Epistemic Pipeline Separation), with the worked consequence that EVal(p)=Supported does not mean Decision=Permit (a governance policy may instead require HumanReview) — epistemic status is explicitly not equivalent to operational authorization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Contr(p) ⇏ ∀q ∈ 𝒫, q. ... Local contradiction ⇏ Global epistemic collapse.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A5 (Non-Explosion): KnowledgeOS explicitly rejects the classical explosion principle as a system rule, requiring contradiction to be scoped and represented rather than collapsing all propositions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 𝒪_core = {ASSERT, LINK, REVISE, RETRACT, ISOLATE}
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the frozen candidate core operation interface (introduce an assertion, establish a relation, change content while preserving history, withdraw standing without erasing history, and restrict propagation of a contradiction or dangerous structure), with full preconditions/postconditions/composition laws deferred to later parts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ABK-1 is a validated candidate-adequate architecture for the target problem class.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly withdraws the earlier claim that ABK-1 is 'the universally unique minimal KnowledgeOS kernel' as circular, replacing it with the weaker, defensible claim that global minimality remains unproven unless the candidate representation space and equivalence relation are formally characterized.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ontology defines what kinds of things KnowledgeOS reasons about. Representation defines how those things are encoded.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the ontology/representation boundary underlying Part II's many-sorted type system (Ent, Val, Attr, Dim, Prop, Asrt, Obs, Evd, Src, Rel, Evt, St, Ctx, Part, Prov, ES, Req, Inq, EC, Pol, Dec, Act), asserting a database/graph/JSON/RDF/object-model representation is never the ontology itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Let D be a value domain and n:D→ℝ a numerical encoding. If no semantic operation corresponding to subtraction is defined on D, then n(x)−n(y) cannot ... be interpreted as a valid semantic difference.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.1 (Representation does not imply arithmetic validity), with proof, establishing that numerical computability of a difference does not by itself establish semantic validity of that difference.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Supports(e,p) ⇏ Truth(p).
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposition 2.1, proved by the type-mismatch argument that support is an epistemic evidence-proposition relation while truth is a semantic proposition-model relation with different domains and meanings; called one of the most important anti-confusion principles in KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Let R:𝕂→X be a representation function. Suppose there exist K1≠K2 such that R(K1)=R(K2). If there exists an inquiry Q such that Answer(Q,K1,Γ)≠Answer(Q,K2,Γ), then R is inadequate for Q,Γ.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.3 (Semantically lossy representation), with proof, generalizing Part I's Theorem 16.1 to the knowledge-state level and formally establishing why representation adequacy must be question-relative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Status_Γ,EC(p)=σ ... We deliberately do not define one universal ordered list such as Unknown<Supported<Proven<Rejected.
b_rows_sample.statement: Epistemic Status is defined as contract- and context-dependent rather than a single universal total order, giving formal meaning to 'unknown' as neither true nor false rather than as a weaker degree of falsity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If Conflict is represented as a local relation on propositions, then the existence of a conflict concerning p does not by itself entail conflict concerning arbitrary q.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.5 (Locality theorem for contradiction), with proof, giving the formal ontological grounding for the non-explosion axiom stated in Part I.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS SHALL NOT treat stored data as knowledge merely because it is stored.
b_rows_sample.statement: Ten Foundational Type Invariants (I1-I10) close Part II — proposition/evidence separation, observation/proposition separation, decision/action separation, epistemic-status/truth separation, identity/state separation, evidence/truth separation, contract relativity, historical preservation, non-explosion, and representation independence — as the boundaries preventing KnowledgeOS from collapsing into an ordinary information system.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth → Evidence → Evaluation → Determination → Decision ... The arrows indicate dependency possibilities, not logical equivalence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines five explicit semantic layers (Truth_M(p), Evid(e,p), Eval(K,p,Gamma), Det(K,p,EC,Gamma), Dec(K,Q,P,A,Gamma)) to prevent classical truth, evidence, uncertainty, contradiction and operational determination from being silently collapsed into one binary logic with metadata.

b_aliases: KnowledgeOS Verified Theory and Mathematical Foundation, Parts I-XVII

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'K_t'

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-4/C-7: ADDRESSED BUT NOT CLOSED ... DV-1 — the one unsafe-direction gap ... the durable copy is written twice after its last all-or-nothing verification ... and re-verified nowhere.
a_rows_sample.statement: AMD6's independent review finds a genuine safety gap (DV-1) in the durability migration plan: the durable authoritative copy is written after its last all-or-nothing verification and never re-verified before the source is removed, so Phase 7's gate could report success while the durable copy is silently incomplete.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'the FIRST record in the authoritative store' is false under the plan's own record vocabulary ... Truth is 'first governance append after the writer switch'
a_rows_sample.statement: Names DV-3: the migration plan's acceptance criterion 17 uses an inaccurate phrase ('first record in the authoritative store', which is literally false because Phase 3 already copied records into it) and must be replaced by 'first governance append after the authority transfer.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Phase 5 remains prohibited ... DV-1 is the critical one because it creates an unsafe path to Phase 7.
a_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes the next lawful sequence after the DV-1..DV-7 findings: register/route a new Architecture correction commission only (not a Governance decision document), then Architecture authors the fix, then a fresh independent Architecture review, then Governance's bounded review, then PO/ARB; Phase 5 must not execute until DV-1 is repaired and reviewed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The durability migration chain (AMD3→AMD6) is literally the test corpus the assurance checker is being built to back-test against, and the checker's job list is literally the migration's own mandated pre-delivery verification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finds that the two seemingly separate work items (cost-optimization/deterministic-assurance, and the durability migration) already share the same evidence base and back-test corpus, so integration is a sequencing/authority problem rather than a new architecture problem; the checker must remain warn-only through Phase 1 to avoid itself becoming a governance object requiring authority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DV-1 = UNSAFE ... Business: Migration must not start yet because there is still a real risk of losing governance evidence.' Not: Migration is almost finished.
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked counterexample showing what an incorrect over-simplified business translation would say versus the correct uncertainty-preserving translation of the DV-1 durability finding.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Decision status is graded, not monolithic: ADR artifact = PROPOSED ('recommends an architecture and decides nothing'); a separate PO/ARB DECISION ACT (2026-08-19) = DECIDED: D1 = B′ adopted, D2 = R-CONFLICT adopt, D3 = existing placement governance.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that decision status must be read as a graded record: an ADR document being PROPOSED does not contradict a separate PO/ARB decision act having already DECIDED specific numbered items from it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D9 | Separation: source of execution vs evidence of execution vs authoritative decision record (B′ relocation, R-CONFLICT) | DECIDED (PO/ARB 2026-08-19, D1–D2) — recorded, not re-decided here
a_rows_sample.statement: Reconciliation-document claim register entry D9: the three-way separation and B′/R-CONFLICT decisions are recorded here as already DECIDED by a separate PO/ARB act, never re-decided by this reconciliation document itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1 RE-HASH ... 1b RECONCILE/DISPOSE DELTA ... 2 READERS ... 3 THE WRITER ← THE AUTHORITY-TRANSFER INSTANT ... 4 RUNTIME DEMOTION MARKER ... 5 STAGING MARKER RETRACTION
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the single canonical Phase-5 slot sequence (1, 1b, 2, 3, 4, 5) with slot 1b's three outcomes (no delta/continue, reconcilable delta/continue, unreconcilable delta/freeze-violation-STOP), replacing two previously-competing enumerations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A MOVE is refused because it would LAUNDER THE QUARANTINE — a post-demotion record lies OUTSIDE the enumeration by definition, so moving it out HIDES the quarantined evidence, makes the source SPURIOUSLY SATISFY criterion 12.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an earlier, inverted justification for forbidding a quarantined record's relocation (previously reasoned as 'would alter the demoted store'); the true reason is that moving it would make a failing Phase-7 comparison spuriously pass.

a_rows_sample.anchor: OPEN-M7 — quarantine disposition — the disposer AND the path ... The one open item that can block the migration's COMPLETION indefinitely.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies that the workflow mechanism has an act class for disposing a quarantine (a governance act) but literally no DISPOSE transition type, so an undisposed quarantine can block migration completion indefinitely by design, not by oversight.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A quarantine is a DOMAIN STATE with a business consequence, not a directory condition. The block is not a tooling limitation to engineer away — it is the aggregate refusing an invalid transition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes quarantine-blocking-completion as a DDD invariant (an aggregate refusing an invalid state transition) rather than a filesystem/tooling limitation to be worked around.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the switch-over record is the FIRST GOVERNANCE APPEND AFTER THE AUTHORITY TRANSFER (⛔ superseded wording: 'that store's first record' — false, not merely imprecise: Phase 3 has already copied governance records into that store.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the acceptance-criterion phrase describing the authoritative store's identifying record: it must read 'first governance append after the authority transfer', not 'that store's first record', because prior copied records already exist there.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the grant count moved 110 → 114 since AMD5, and it is C-4's premise observed live: those four grants are AMD6's OWN commission, appended by P-1 into the corpus the migration freezes and hashes.
a_rows_sample.statement: A self-referential observation: the ongoing governance work authorizing this very amendment is itself appended to the corpus the migration plan proposes to freeze, meaning a literal freeze would have had to prohibit the act that authorized the amendment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ELIGIBILITY OUTCOME AS RECORDED: bc1b47ef - AUTHORING ELIGIBLE, REVIEWING BARRED, ACCEPTING BARRED ... A FRESH INDEPENDENT ARCHITECTURE PROCESS - REVIEWING ... REQUIRED.
a_rows_sample.statement: A registered grant explicitly restores a producer's authoring eligibility while permanently barring it from reviewing or accepting its own amendment (AMD6), which the reviewer here reads directly from the record rather than inferring.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A reviewer checking only the two names it was handed would have PASSED this gate and proceeded ... this is exactly why the same commission forbids hand-copied grant lists: the chat-supplied exclusion set was narrower than the governed one.
a_rows_sample.statement: Demonstrates the failure mode of trusting a prompt-supplied exclusion list rather than the governed record: the chat-supplied set of two barred names missed a fourth clause that fires on a registered grant covering the same performer under a different role in this same chain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1 PO/ARB starts a FRESH Architecture session ... 2 that session DECLARES its own identity ... 3 GOVERNANCE ... appends REGISTER ... then HANDOFF ... 4 START recorded with THIS PO/ARB act as its humanAct ... 5 the fresh reviewer consumes G-…-DV-CORRECTION-READING-ORDER as its index
a_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes the exact five-step lawful sequence that would unblock the deadlocked reviewer-appointment problem without a barred process appointing its own judge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: THE REVIEWER MUST BE A FRESH INDEPENDENT ARCHITECTURE PROCESS ... Satisfied on the measurement in §2.2: this is a process with no registered role in the chain.
a_rows_sample.statement: Demonstrates the independence-verification method in practice: enumerate every process occurrence across all transitions and grants in the aggregate plus a whole-repository grep, and treat zero occurrences as the only admissible basis for eligibility.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the reviewer must not be its own registrar — the same reason bc1b47ef refused to appoint its own judge, applied to the other end of the same edge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the 'a barred process must not appoint its own judge' principle to its symmetric case: an eligible candidate reviewer must also not register/hand-off its own assignment, since separation is the entire point of the lane.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the eligibility set keeps narrowing — every candidate reviewer that declares eligibility and is then not started adds one more name to it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Observes a structural risk pattern: repeatedly declaring and abandoning candidate reviewers without recording a START permanently shrinks the pool of processes still eligible to review, since each attempt itself becomes a disqualifying prior-participation fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: independence is not transferable: an assignment whose recorded evidence names a8ce5a39 cannot be discharged by 8a525719 without the record asserting something false about who did the work.
a_rows_sample.statement: Names a second-order independence failure distinct from personal ineligibility: a genuinely independent process cannot discharge a review under a workflow lane whose registered execution context names a different process, since INV-ATTR-1 means the engine itself would never detect the substitution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rel(kos, ai, "Bootstraps and constrains AI sessions") Rel(ai, kos, "Executes assigned work under grants")
b_rows_sample.statement: The KnowledgeOS system bootstraps and constrains AI sessions, and the AI/Agent Runtime executes assigned work under grants -- a two-directional relation between the governed platform and executing AI sessions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Component(workflow, "Workflow Engine", "Governed workflow", "Grants, assignments, handoffs, mutation ownership and transitions")
b_rows_sample.statement: The Workflow Engine component is defined as owning grants, assignments, handoffs, mutation ownership and transitions -- the governed-workflow mechanism later referred to throughout the batch as BC-7 / the workflow-state engine.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rel(review, verification, "Routes independent verification")
b_rows_sample.statement: A Review Engine component is proposed whose role is to route independent verification and preserve role separation, distinct from the Verification Engine component itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ContainerDb(estate, "Knowledge / Workflow Estate", "Git + governed records", "Architecture artifacts, ADRs, reports, workflow JSON, source and tests")
b_rows_sample.statement: A single durable 'Knowledge / Workflow Estate' store (git + governed records) is proposed as the persistence layer for architecture artifacts, ADRs, reports, workflow JSON, source and tests.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The architecture lane S4 was HANDED_OFF at seq 5 and NEVER returned to ACTIVE
b_rows_sample.statement: Programmatic check of the workflow record shows the architecture lane producing Amendment 1 held mutation ownership at HANDOFF but never received a START/CONTINUATION afterward, meaning Amendment 1 was produced by a lane not verifiably ACTIVE on the record -- distinguished from whether its claims are independently assessable (they are).

b_rows_sample.anchor: every invariant BC-7 owns is MECHANICALLY enforced; almost every invariant outside BC-7 is DECLARED ONLY. INFERRED: the platform's assurance is strong exactly where it is executable and weak exactly where it is prose -- and a role model is prose.
b_rows_sample.statement: The discovery's core structural result: BC-7's invariants (I-1 single mutation owner, I-2 HANDOFF+human START, I-3 sticky STOPPED, G-1 closure is a governance act, G-2 single writer for the Authority State) are all mechanically enforced, while almost every invariant outside BC-7 (R-34 producer!=acceptor, INV-ATTR-2 separation, AIP-11 frozen-artifact supersession, AIP-14 Product Primacy) is declared only, with no enforcement mechanism.

b_rows_sample.anchor: this verification lane has no START on the record, so this report is produced off-record, the second occurrence at the "Verification #3" slot in this estate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding X-2: this verification's own workflow lane has no recorded START, meaning the report is produced off-record -- the second occurrence of the same lifecycle-gap pattern at a 'Verification #3' slot across this estate, classified as a platform gap (bearing on C-10/knowledge-distribution and G-3) rather than a defect of Correction #2.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Correction #2 finished its work and said so in the artifact, but its lane never handed off -- it still held mutation ownership when this act arrived.
b_rows_sample.statement: A recurring delivery/record gap pattern is recorded: an artifact states it is delivered, but the lane that produced it never performed the corresponding HANDOFF transition, so the workflow record lags the actual work; Governance performs the handoff now rather than back-dating it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X-2 is a live blocker ... the work item's mutationOwner is None: seq 14 handed off to a lane that then never STARTed, so ownership was released and never taken up. Consequently no lane can hand off
b_rows_sample.statement: A workflow lane that is HANDED_OFF to but never STARTed leaves mutationOwner as None, mechanically blocking every subsequent lane's handoff (Inv C requires the current mutation owner to hand off) -- a live, measured blocker rather than a theoretical one, confirmed by probing a scratch copy of the record.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Option A -- transcribing the missing START -- is not available to Governance. A transcription records a human act that was given. No such act exists in this lane's record, and Governance may not supply one.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance determines it cannot itself transcribe a missing human START act, because a transcription records a fact (that a human act occurred) which only the PO/ARB can supply; Governance instead retains the report as evidence produced off-record, leaving option A open to the PO/ARB at any time.

b_rows_sample.anchor: restoring append-only history is itself a history edit, two lanes were writing this file the same day, and a restoration performed without authority would repeat the very defect it repairs.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance declines to restore 73 deleted lines from an append-only session log, reasoning that restoring append-only history is itself a history-edit and could repeat the defect it would fix; it instead recommends preserving current history with an explicit recovery-commit pointer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The record is not broken. It is exactly ONE HUMAN ACT short.
b_rows_sample.statement: Diagnosis: the entire workflow chain is blocked by exactly one missing human START act; once the PO/ARB affirms it occurred, Governance transcribes the START (preserving on the record's face that the artifact predates the transition) and the blocked handoff chain unblocks in one move.

b_rows_sample.anchor: There is an important distinction between the role model and the workflow state machine. The roles tell us who may act; the lifecycle tells us what happens and in what order.
b_rows_sample.statement: A foundational distinction is drawn between the role model (who may act) and the workflow state machine (what happens and in what order), presented as two separate but related layers of the governed AI engineering lifecycle.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A deliverable being produced is not the same thing as its lifecycle being closed.
b_rows_sample.statement: A critical rule surfaced from the BC-7 history: a deliverable being produced (content exists) is not the same thing as its lifecycle being closed (the governed record reflects it) -- the earliest statement in this batch of the delivery/record gap pattern that recurs dozens of times in later documents.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A lane cannot hand off work the record does not show it ever started. ... Governance will not manufacture the START, and will not record the bootstrap form from: null
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance refuses a directed HANDOFF because the predecessor lane, though it produced a delivered artifact, was never STARTed on the record and therefore holds no mutation ownership; refuses both manufacturing a START and using a null-predecessor bootstrap form, because either would falsely assert something about the record.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the START sits at seq 25, later in the log than the work it authorized. This is recorded deliberately and is not an error to be tidied ... no historical ordering is invented
b_rows_sample.statement: A governance transcription convention is established: when a human act is confirmed after the fact, its transition is recorded at its true (later) sequence position, not back-dated to appear before the work it authorized -- the record states explicitly that the artifact predates the transcription.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A later act is not automatically a supersession. Act B may be an amendment superseding Act A, a re-issue that crossed with it, or a duplicate. ... Until Governance disposes, a0b61305 remains the recorded DECIDED text
b_rows_sample.statement: A general governance principle: a later act arriving on an already-DECIDED slot is not automatically read as superseding it; until Governance explicitly disposes of the relationship (amendment, re-issue, or duplicate), the earlier recorded DECIDED text remains authoritative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: acts and records have crossed four times -- seq-16 and seq-22 transcriptions, the seq-21 producer designation, the S4b missing START, and now two D1 acts.
b_rows_sample.statement: A cumulative pattern is named explicitly: the record and the governed acts on this work item have crossed (diverged and required reconciliation) four separate times, treated as a recurring structural pattern each disposed individually by Governance rather than absorbed silently.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Handing off from S5 would set S5 to HANDED_OFF, misrepresenting an OUTSTANDING verification as concluded. ... a lane with no recorded handoff can never legally START. ... Registering an assignment now would create a permanently unreachable lane.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance declines to register a new workflow lane for D5, because the current mutation owner (S5, an outstanding/refused verification) would need to hand off, which would misrepresent that verification as concluded; instead D5 proceeds as a PO/ARB-directed act, deferring the lane-creation question until S5's disposition is settled.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HANDED_OFF means the lane RELEASED MUTATION OWNERSHIP. It does NOT mean the verification was performed. a lane that refused on independence now reads, in the state column, indistinguishably from lanes that finished their work.
b_rows_sample.statement: A workflow-engine state-vocabulary risk is named: the HANDED_OFF state denotes only that mutation ownership was released, not that any verification, consumption, or acceptance occurred -- so a lane that refused on independence grounds becomes indistinguishable, in the raw state column, from a lane that actually finished its work, requiring explicit clarification for any later reader.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Authority, Decision, Policy, Exception, Knowledge, Claim, Evidence, Observation, FitnessRule, Verification, Finding, Recommendation, Authorization, Action, Agent, Session, Artifact, RuntimeState
a_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 137 (The KnowledgeOS Domain Model): poses the question 'what must exist in the model for the assurance lifecycle to be expressible?' and lists eighteen candidate semantic objects around which the first consolidated domain model will center, from which genuine aggregates, value objects, and cross-context references will be identified — explicitly not yet a database/class design.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Aggregates + Commands + Domain Events + CrossContext Contracts.
a_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 138 (Aggregates, Commands and Domain Events): poses the question of which concepts can change independently, which state transitions require invariants, and what commands/events cross bounded-context boundaries, to translate the semantic model into an implementable DDD architecture without prematurely choosing databases/microservices/frameworks.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Aggregates, Entities, Value Objects, Domain Events and Invariants. What each Aggregate is allowed to change.
a_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 146 (Golden Trace -> Domain Model): formalizes the Golden Trace's exposed objects into tactical DDD constructs, with the critical decisions being which objects are Aggregates, transaction boundaries, which IDs are Value Objects, which relationships belong inside an Aggregate vs only in the Graph, which events cross bounded-context boundaries, and what each Aggregate may change — to implement the first Golden Trace without collapsing bounded contexts into one object model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS = {Knowledge, Context, Inquiry, Authority, Decision, Action, Observation, Evidence, Verification, Governance}. What is the smallest model that still preserves all required invariants? What are the true bounded contexts and aggregate boundaries?
b_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 157 (KnowledgeOS Domain Model Reduction): the next question is the minimum irreducible domain model, testing which of ten candidate concepts are actually entities, value objects, aggregates, domain services, bounded contexts, or merely relationships, explicitly warning against over-modeling after an accumulated rich architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Layer 1 Epistemic Constitution (claim/evidence/knowledge/determination/authority/provenance/verification meanings). Layer 2 Operating Model (Actor→Knowledge→Action operation). Layer 3 Implementation Architecture (services/aggregates/APIs/events/repositories/agent adapters/registries/databases/hooks/runtime). Ontology → Operating Model → Implementation, not Technology → Services → retroactive semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the three-layer architecture ordering established so far and opens Step 157 (KnowledgeOS Domain Model & Bounded Context Validation): a rigorous DDD test of which operating-model concepts are Entities, Value Objects, Aggregates, Domain Events, Policies, Bounded Contexts, or must remain outside the domain model — testing whether the actual implementation architecture is consistent with the established epistemic and operating constitution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Good conceptual model ⇏ Good DDD model. Six questions: identity? own lifecycle? own invariants? change independently? clear domain meaning? belong to one bounded context?
b_rows_sample.statement: States the six-question DDD test distinguishing Entity/Aggregate candidates from Value Object/Domain Service/Policy/Domain Event/external-concept/implementation-detail classifications, preventing every noun from becoming a class.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS = Network of bounded semantic models, not one KnowledgeAggregate containing Claims/Evidence/Sources/Decisions/Actions/Users/Verification/Governance.
b_rows_sample.statement: Makes the strong correction rejecting a single giant Knowledge aggregate, presenting a candidate six-bounded-context landscape (Knowledge, Inquiry, Governance, Assurance, Action, with Evidence feeding Assurance) explicitly as a candidate landscape, not a final decomposition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Context: manage governed representations of engineering knowledge and their provenance, owning KnowledgeClaim/KnowledgeSource/Provenance/KnowledgeVersion/KnowledgeRelationship — not approval, production execution, voting, infrastructure execution, or agent sessions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Knowledge bounded context's responsibility and explicit non-ownership boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeClaim is an Entity (Claim_A(t1) and Claim_A(t2) must remain distinguishable across its lifecycle). Proposition is a Value Object (KnowledgeClaim ⊃ Proposition). Scope is a Value Object {System,Environment,Organization,Domain,TemporalBoundary}. Validity ≠ Version (version=which representation; validity=during what domain period applicable).
b_rows_sample.statement: Classifies KnowledgeClaim as Entity with its schema (ClaimId,Proposition,Subject,Scope,EpistemicStatus,Validity,ProvenanceRef,SourceRef,Version), and classifies Proposition/Scope/Validity individually, distinguishing Validity from Version with worked timestamps (recordedAt/validFrom/validTo).

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeSource ≠ Artifact — a source may be an artifact, but not every artifact is epistemically a source.
b_rows_sample.statement: Classifies KnowledgeSource as an Entity (examples: Architecture Constitution, ADR, Repository, Infrastructure system, Board decision, external standard, human observation) with an explicit Source≠Artifact distinction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Inquiry is an Aggregate Root (owns invariants like Inquiry.status, controls lifecycle OPEN→INVESTIGATING→DETERMINED→CLOSED). Inquiry does not own Evidence — Inquiry→EvidenceRequirement→references Evidence, not Inquiry→Evidence[] as transactional ownership.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Inquiry aggregate schema (InquiryId,Intent,Subject,Scope,Actor,Context,Questions,EvidenceRequirements,Status,OutcomeReferences), its Aggregate Root status, and the subtle boundary that it references rather than transactionally owns evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Context = assembled view over governed knowledge, not something that owns all its constituent objects. ContextSnapshot is a Value Object/immutable projection enabling deterministic replay: reconstruct Inquiry+ContextSnapshot+Knowledge versions+Evidence versions+Method+Agent identity to reproduce the epistemic input. ContextSnapshot → Reproducibility.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines the prior Context concept, correcting the assumption that Context owns its constituent objects, and formalizes the reproducibility guarantee this projection model provides for assurance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence domain purpose: represent observations and evidentiary material with provenance and method (Observation, Evidence, EvidenceSource, AcquisitionMethod, EvidenceQuality) — not simply a document store. Observation = what was observed, not what we think it means. Evidence has many consumers (Observation O17 supports Determination D1 and contradicts Determination D2) — argues against embedding evidence inside a determination aggregate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence bounded context and classifies Observation (Entity/immutable record) vs Evidence (may have many consumers, distinct from a single Observation) with a worked multi-consumer example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance answers: does available evidence justify the required conclusion under the defined method? Determination is a strong Aggregate Root candidate {DeterminationId,Proposition,Method,EvidenceReferences,Result,EpistemicStatus,Actor,ContextSnapshot} — invariant: cannot claim evidentiary support without referencing the evidence/method it depends on. DRAFT→PROPOSED→FINALIZED, immutable after finalization; superseded via Determination D1→SupersededBy→D2, giving epistemic history.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Assurance bounded context and the Determination aggregate in full, including its finalization-immutability and supersession pattern.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Verification(Proposition,Evidence,Method,Rule)→Result ∈ {VERIFIED,NOT_VERIFIED,INCONCLUSIVE,NOT_APPLICABLE}. Deterministic assurance: Rule+Machine-observable state→Result. Interpretive assurance: Evidence+Method+Domain judgment→Determination — should not be forced into the same implementation model.
b_rows_sample.statement: Models Verification as a specialized assurance operation and formally separates deterministic from interpretive assurance modes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Governance: establish, approve, authorize, supersede and govern decisions within defined authority scopes (Decision, Authority, Policy, Mandate, Approval, Exception, Delegation). Decision is Entity/Aggregate Root referencing Determination/Authority/Scope/DecisionBasis/DecisionTime/Validity but not owning the Determination.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Governance bounded context and the Decision aggregate's reference-not-ownership relationship to Determination.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Person ≠ Role ≠ Authority ≠ Delegation. AuthorityGrant{GrantId,Actor,AuthorityType,Scope,Validity,DelegatedBy,Constraints} — makes authority explicit and auditable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires careful DDD treatment distinguishing an organizational role (e.g. Architecture Board) from a Person from an AuthorityGrant, with the AuthorityGrant schema.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Exception is not 'rule=false' but an explicitly governed deviation: Rule→Violation/Deviation→Exception Request→Authority→Exception Granted. Exception = Exception(Scope,Time,Conditions,Authority) — validFrom/validTo/scope/conditions/authority, integrating with the temporal model.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Exception as a first-class, temporally-scoped governed deviation concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Action: translate authorized decisions into consequential actions and record execution effects (Action, Authorization, Execution, ExecutionResult, Observation). Authorization ≠ Action (Authorization permits, Action is what happens). Action ≠ Execution ≠ TechnicalCommand — three semantic layers ('Migrate Nexus' vs 'run migration workflow #47' vs 'podman ...'). Observation belongs after Execution, preventing RequestedEffect=ActualEffect assumption.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Action bounded context and its three-layer semantic separation with the Action->Execution->Observation ordering explicitly preventing the assumption that requested and actual effect are equal.

b_rows_sample.anchor: InquiryOpened, ContextEstablished, ClaimCreated, ClaimSuperseded, EvidenceCaptured, DeterminationProposed, DeterminationFinalized, DecisionMade, AuthorityGranted, ExceptionGranted, ActionAuthorized, ActionExecuted, ObservationCaptured, VerificationCompleted, KnowledgeSuperseded. Command ≠ Event ('Verify Nexus backup coverage' vs 'NexusBackupVerificationCompleted').
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists fifteen domain events useful for the audit/trace model, restating Command≠Event with a worked example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Production changes require explicit authorization' and 'architecture decisions above risk threshold X require Board approval' are Policies, operating across aggregates without becoming giant orchestration objects. ContextResolutionService, AuthorityResolutionService, EvidenceEvaluationService, ProvenanceResolutionService may be Domain Services — but a KnowledgeService containing 80% of domain logic is a warning sign.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies Domain Policies and candidate Domain Services, warning against an overloaded generic service class absorbing most domain logic.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KNOWLEDGE{KnowledgeClaim,KnowledgeSource,KnowledgeVersion}; INQUIRY{Inquiry}; EVIDENCE{Observation,Evidence}; ASSURANCE{Determination,Verification}; GOVERNANCE{Decision,AuthorityGrant,Exception}; ACTION{Authorization,Action} — with Provenance/ContextSnapshot/Policy/DomainEvents crossing boundaries through explicit contracts.
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents the consolidated candidate aggregate map across six bounded contexts plus cross-cutting concerns.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KNOWLEDGE -claims/sources-> INQUIRY -evidence need-> EVIDENCE -evidence-> ASSURANCE -determination-> GOVERNANCE -authorization-> ACTION -observation-> ASSURANCE — 'the first version I would be comfortable calling a DDD context map rather than merely a workflow.'
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents the DDD context map connecting all six bounded contexts through their relationship edges.
