a_rows_sample.anchor: EXPERIMENT ID KR-BRIDGE-01-ZERO-PRESERVATION-2026-09 ... Determine whether there is any reproducible empirical or structural relationship between: A. elimination/Transformation-relative Zero, B. representation preservation/adequacy. WITHOUT assuming that Zero is a preservation criterion. ... The exp
a_rows_sample.statement: Commissions KR-BRIDGE-01-ZERO-PRESERVATION-2026-09, a bridge/falsification experiment explicitly designed to determine whether there is any reproducible relationship between elimination/Transformation-relative Zero and representation-preservation adequacy without assuming Zero is a preservation criterion, required to remain capable of falsifying the hypothesized relationship, and prohibited from constructing an algebra, pre-selecting a carrier, modifying Theory v1.2, creating Theory v1.3, selecting a kernel operator, or merging KR-ZERO and KR-REP-REDUCTION into one formalism.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO: ~89.7% singleton-determined levels ... ~8.2% irreducible levels ... Does NOT establish Zero as a preservation criterion. KR-REP-REDUCTION: R5 adequate, R4 inadequate ... Found no observed Zero/boundary association in that experiment. Does NOT establish a KR-ZERO law. ... These experiments a
a_rows_sample.statement: Summarizes the existing empirical baseline the bridge experiment builds on: KR-ZERO (89.7% singleton-determined, 8.2% irreducible, does not establish Zero as a preservation criterion) and KR-REP-REDUCTION (R5 adequate/R4 inadequate, no observed Zero/boundary association), framed as complementary but analytically independent results whose missing bridge the new experiment must test rather than assume.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H0: Zero and preservation are not systematically related in the tested regime. H1: Zero is associated with preservation under specified conditions. H2: Zero is predictive of preservation only under particular transformation/observable/contract configurations. H3: Any apparent relationship is explain
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies four competing hypotheses to be distinguished -- H0 no systematic relationship, H1 association under specified conditions, H2 predictive only under particular transformation/observable/contract configurations, H3 apparent relationship explained by a confounding factor (transformation class, contract, observable, redundancy, representation regime) -- with an explicit instruction not to privilege H1, and defines success as producing a clear positive or negative result regarding the tested relationship.

a_rows_sample.anchor: USE A PARALLEL REPRESENTATION FAMILY. Do NOT use only a deterministic sequential chain. A sequential chain ... has a data-processing constraint H(Q|Rn) <= H(Q|R(n-1)) and therefore cannot test non-monotone adequacy. The present experiment requires independently generated representations: Ra = Ta(D),
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates the critical design rule that the bridge experiment use a parallel representation family (independently generated representations Ra=Ta(D), Rb=Tb(D), neither a deterministic function of the other) rather than only a deterministic sequential chain, since a sequential chain's data-processing constraint H(Q|Rn)<=H(Q|R(n-1)) structurally prevents testing non-monotone adequacy -- directly addressing the H-C category error found in the prior KR-REP-REDUCTION reviews.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The mathematical carrier must be the minimum structure required by the actual experiment. Do not declare: set, graph, hypergraph, lattice, matroid, closure system, rewriting system, category, algebra as the carrier before the experiment. ... clearly distinguish: experimental carrier, mathematical ca
a_rows_sample.statement: Prohibits declaring any specific mathematical carrier (set, graph, hypergraph, lattice, matroid, closure system, rewriting system, category, algebra) before the experiment runs, requiring the carrier to be the minimum structure the experiment actually needs, and mandates keeping experimental carrier, mathematical carrier, and future KnowledgeOS knowledge representation explicitly distinct with no unevidenced transfer between them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use a finite structured source D ... rich enough to permit: redundancy, relational dependence, context dependence, individually removable elements, jointly non-removable groups, preservation and information-loss cases. ... For every source case store D, Q(D), contract parameters, transformation para
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the source data D to be a finite, deterministically-seeded structured source rich enough to permit redundancy, relational dependence, context dependence, individually removable elements, jointly non-removable groups, and both preservation and information-loss cases, with complete persistence of every source case's D, Q(D), contract parameters, transformation parameters, Zero ground truth, every representation, adequacy result, and decoder result, so no result depends on regenerated or hidden data.

a_rows_sample.anchor: At minimum construct representations with: R_A: information-preserving transformation, R_B: controlled lossy transformation, R_C: redundancy-removing transformation, R_D: relational/context-sensitive transformation. ... Do not optimize transformations after seeing results.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires at minimum four independently constructed representations -- R_A (information-preserving), R_B (controlled lossy), R_C (redundancy-removing), R_D (relational/context-sensitive) -- each fully specified (transformation ID, mathematical definition, input/output type, deterministic/random status, seed, provenance, expected information effect, contract dependencies) before results are examined, with no post-hoc optimization of transformations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Define Q BEFORE generating representations. ... Adequate(R) iff Q is recoverable from R. Operationally measure both empirical conditional information Hhat(Q|R) and exact semantic violation count Nviol ... Do not treat Hhat(Q|R)=0 as proof that population H(Q|R)=0.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the preservation target Q to be defined before representations are generated, with adequacy defined as Q being recoverable from R, measured operationally via both empirical conditional information Hhat(Q|R) and an exact semantic violation count Nviol, while never treating the empirical Hhat(Q|R)=0 as proof of the population-level H(Q|R)=0.

a_rows_sample.statement: Defines four mutually exclusive possible outcome classes for the experiment: A) no relationship observed (does not prove universal independence); B) conditional relationship under particular configurations (must not be generalized); C) robust relationship surviving transformations/observables/contracts/controls (the only case permitting a formal bridge hypothesis for a new experiment); D) design failure, in which case results must not be interpreted theoretically and the experiment must be revised.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Pi_value_set was declared to read the value field. Under T_D_relational its value is computed from rank, and rank is produced by ordering values within a tag group -- so the observable was in fact carried by tag, the very field Q reads. It did not know this. Neither did I, and I wrote it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports a KR-BRIDGE-02 (Pi x Q grid) finding that the observable Pi_value_set, declared to read only the value field, actually derives its value under transformation T_D_relational from a rank computed by ordering values within a tag group -- so it was in fact carried by the tag field, the very field the inquiry Q reads, an undetected coupling that violates the target/observable-independence discipline established for the bridge experiments.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the corrected map was still wrong: Pi_arity reads no field by declaration, and after T_C_dedup it reads v -- because arity is a function of which records survive, and membership is decided by a field. A perturbation test found this; reading the code did not.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports a second, subtler provenance error even after the first was corrected: Pi_arity, declared to read no field, actually reads the v field after transformation T_C_dedup because arity depends on which records survive deduplication and survival is decided by that field, a coupling found only by a perturbation test (changing one input field and observing which outputs move) and not by reading the implementation code.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The structural point, stripped of its soteriology: the agent's account of its own activity is not the activity. Pi reports {v}. Pi is in fact carried by {v, tag}. Its self-description is sincere and wrong, and its wrongness is not visible from inside itself -- it is visible only from the transformat
b_rows_sample.statement: Reads Gita 3.27 as corroborating the shape of the KR-BRIDGE-02 failure: an observable's declared self-description (Pi reports {v}) can be sincere yet wrong (Pi is actually carried by {v,tag}), and this wrongness is not visible from inside the declaration itself, only from the transformation that actually constitutes the observable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: gahana karmano gatih -- 4.17 -- 'the way of action is deep / impenetrable.' Not mysticism here: dependency structure is not surface-readable. Two of my three provenance maps were wrong, and I was reading the code that produced them each time.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reads Gita 4.17 ('the way of action is deep/impenetrable') non-mystically as corroborating that dependency structure is not surface-readable: two of three declared provenance maps in this cycle were wrong despite reading the very code that produced them each time.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Effective-read closure: an observable's read-set must be computed through the transformation's provenance, never declared. b_rows_sample.statement: Registers candidate FR-003 (effective-read closure: an observable's read-set must be computed through the transformation's actual provenance, never taken from its declaration), established by the KR-BRIDGE-02 experiment itself with the lens only naming it after the fact; registers 'declaration != verification' as a standing experimental obligation [PROP] with two independent occurrences now (KR-BRIDGE-01's T_B label mismatch and KR-BRIDGE-02's provenance failures), explicitly noting two occurrences is not promotion per ES-006.1; and rejects both non-doership as a kernel stance (no mechanical content) and 'action's depth' as an argument for interpretive humility in the kernel (legitimate only as a reason to test, which is already an obligation).

b_rows_sample.anchor: We have experimentally separated three things that we previously tended to mix together: information elimination, preservation of a business inquiry, and successful realization by a decoder. Eliminability != Preservation != Realization.
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms the three-way separation of Eliminability, Preservation, and Realization as the strongest result of the KR-REP-REDUCTION/KR-ZERO assessment, restating the formal three questions (can the business question be answered: H(Q|R)=0; can something be eliminated: Zero_{T,Pi}; can the decoder recover the answer: O(R)=Q(D)).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Every future mathematical statement in KnowledgeOS must carry its epistemic status: Definition, Theorem, Corollary, Empirical Result, Proposition, Conjecture, Refuted, or Open. That is what will allow us to turn this from an interesting research program into a genuinely rigorous mathematical theory
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes making it a permanent methodological rule that every future KnowledgeOS mathematical statement carry an explicit epistemic-status tag (Definition, Theorem, Corollary, Empirical Result, Proposition, Conjecture, Refuted, or Open), to prevent accidentally promoting an experiment into a theorem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The original read-disjointness gate was unsound. It checked declared source-field reads, but transformations can derive output fields from other fields. The corrected gate has to operate on the actual transformed representation and be verified empirically.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports that KR-BRIDGE-02 discovered its own original read-disjointness gate was unsound because it checked declared source-field reads while transformations can derive output fields from other fields (matching the Pi_value_set/tag coupling found in the companion Gita study), requiring the corrected gate to operate on the actual transformed representation and be verified empirically rather than by declaration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The first adjudication criterion was wrong. Marginal RD simply rediscovered the redundancy confounding already identified in BRIDGE-01. A conditional bridge has to survive within redundancy strata, using the Mantel-Haenszel risk difference.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports that KR-BRIDGE-02's first adjudication criterion (marginal risk difference) was wrong because it simply rediscovered the redundancy confounding already identified in BRIDGE-01, requiring instead that a conditional bridge survive within redundancy strata using the Mantel-Haenszel risk difference.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No admissible (Pi,Q,T) produced a substantive within-stratum Zero-preservation relationship replicated on both train and test. ... the document does not establish a universal 'no-bridge law.' b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the KR-BRIDGE-02 headline finding after both corrections: no admissible (Pi,Q,T) configuration produced a substantive within-stratum Zero-preservation relationship replicated on both train and test, but this is explicitly not a universal 'no-bridge law' since only 31 of 112 candidate cells were actually searched after applying the increasingly strict gate and informativeness requirements, scoping the negative result to the tested region only.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Pi-family size != mechanism count. After deduplication, value multiset, value set, and arity become mutually determined, so several apparently different Pi observations are actually the same mechanism under that transformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a new methodological finding to preserve in the theory: Pi-family size does not equal mechanism count -- after a deduplication transformation, the observables value-multiset, value-set, and arity become mutually determined, so several apparently distinct Pi observations collapse into the same underlying mechanism under that transformation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The governance status is exactly right: experiment + audit, not yet adjudicated theory. The document explicitly keeps Theory v1.2 frozen and says nothing here has yet been promoted into Theory v1.3.
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms KR-BRIDGE-02's governance status as experiment plus audit, not yet adjudicated theory, with Theory v1.2 remaining frozen and nothing promoted to Theory v1.3.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would treat BRIDGE-02 as a significant methodological strengthening of the research program, especially because the experiment caught its own measurement/gating assumptions twice rather than merely producing another numerical result.
b_rows_sample.statement: Judges KR-BRIDGE-02 a significant methodological strengthening of the research program precisely because it caught its own measurement/gating assumptions wrong twice (the read-disjointness gate and the marginal-RD adjudication criterion) rather than merely producing another numerical result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: BRIDGE-02 was designed specifically to attack the remaining Pi/Q gap identified here, while also discovering that the original read-disjointness gate itself was insufficient. b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms the now-clear overall research sequence KR-ZERO -> KR-REP-REDUCTION -> BRIDGE-01 -> BRIDGE-02, with BRIDGE-02 having been designed specifically to attack the remaining Pi/Q gap left by BRIDGE-01, under the unchanged governance rule Experiment -> Audit -> Adjudication -> Theory v1.3 and Theory v1.2 remaining frozen.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Eliminability does not predict Preservation
b_rows_sample.statement: Four experiments of increasing power (H-RR2 boundary-crossing Zero rate 0.0377 vs 0.0426; KR-BRIDGE-01 marginal RD=-0.363 fully explained by redundancy confounding; KR-BRIDGE-02 H1 not refuted; KR-BRIDGE-03 at 13x informative strata, H1 still not refuted, surviving cells 14->1) converge on the same negative finding, stable under a 13-fold power increase.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Π and Q must read disjoint fields, and disjointness must be discharged on the triple (Π, Q, T), not the pair (Π, Q).
b_rows_sample.statement: An anti-circularity requirement (candidate FR-003) is proposed: read-disjointness of Pi and Q must be verified on the triple (Pi,Q,T) because T can derive an output field Pi reads from sources Pi never declared; two concrete KR-BRIDGE-02 failures (a rank field secretly shared with Q's tag field, and an arity observable secretly reading value via deduplication survivorship) show declaration is not verification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No Zero/preservation bridge exists for read-disjoint (Π, Q).
b_rows_sample.statement: Standing conjecture with an explicit refutation condition (one substantive, replicating, gate-clean cell with |MH-RD|>=0.01 on both splits); stated so it can be attacked rather than hardening into an assumption.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Read-disjointness must be discharged on the triple (Π, Q, T) and verified empirically.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-003, CANDIDATE this cycle, established by KR-BRIDGE-02 §2 catching a false positive (MH-RD=-0.155, replicating) that a hand-inspected provenance map (wrong twice) would otherwise have let through; needs a second independent adopter before promotion per ES-006.1.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero predicts preservation [NEG] — 4 independent tests
b_rows_sample.statement: Refuted claims about the bridge: Zero does not predict preservation (4 independent tests), Zero does not mark the reduction boundary, admissibility is a property of (Pi,Q,T) not (Pi,Q), read-disjointness cannot be established by declaration, and neither flattening the redundancy distribution nor raising population size increases informative strata.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The one substantial effect in the entire grid was an artifact of shared reads.
b_rows_sample.statement: KR-BRIDGE-02's instrument failed twice before reporting anything: first a marginal-RD adjudication falsely reported 'H2 SUPPORTED, 27/27 replicate' (re-finding the known confounder), then a naive read-disjointness gate let through an inadmissible cell (MH-RD=-0.155, replicating) caused by rank=f(value,tag) leaking into Pi; a second, corrected gate was itself found unsound by perturbation testing (Pi_arity effectively reading value via dedup survivorship), yielding the rule 'admissibility is a property of the TRIPLE (Pi,Q,T), never of the pair' and 'declaration is not verification.'

a_rows_sample.statement: Defines four mutually exclusive possible outcome classes for the experiment: A) no relationship observed (does not prove universal independence); B) conditional relationship under particular configurations (must not be generalized); C) robust relationship surviving transformations/observables/contracts/controls (the only case permitting a formal bridge hypothesis for a new experiment); D) design failure, in which case results must not be interpreted theoretically and the experiment must be revised.

b_rows_sample.statement: Derives, via the data-processing inequality applied to the deterministic chain Q->R_n->R_{n-1} (each R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n)), that H(Q|R_5)<=H(Q|R_4)<=H(Q|R_3)<=H(Q|R_2), i.e. adequacy cannot recover later in a deterministic sequential chain; reclassifies the original hypothesis H-C (that adequacy could become non-monotone, e.g. R3 adequate again after R4 inadequate) not as empirically falsified by the data but as structurally ill-posed/a priori inapplicable to this experiment class, recommending the frozen label read '[THEORY/NEG] H-C was ill-posed for the specified sequential deterministic chain; the data-processing inequality makes non-monotone conditional-entropy adequacy impossible' rather than 'H-C refuted a priori', on the ground that a priori impossibility and empirical falsification are epistemically distinct.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sequential family: D -> R5 -> R4 -> R3 -> R2 ... No recovery is possible. Parallel family: D -> R_A, D -> R_B, D -> R_C ... Non-monotone comparative behavior is possible here.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a distinction proposed to become part of the theory: a 'sequential family' of representations (each derived deterministically from the previous one) where H(Q|R) is provably monotone with no recovery possible, versus a 'parallel family' of independently constructed representations from the same source D, where one representation can destroy a distinction while another independently preserves it, so non-monotone comparative adequacy is possible; frames this as the difference between monotonicity along a sequential information-reducing chain and comparative adequacy across independently constructed representations, expected to matter when investigating alternative knowledge representations later.

b_rows_sample.statement: Reports hypothesis H-E's result that empirical Hhat(R_n) exceeds Hhat(Q) at every level of the chain (R5=15.042 through R2=7.170, versus Hhat(Q)=5.0098), matching the expected theoretical lower-bound relationship under the relevant assumptions, and endorses treating this as empirical consistency with the theoretical bound rather than as a proof.

b_rows_sample.statement: Reports hypothesis H-RR2's negative result: measured Zero rates across the chain (3.77%, 4.26%, 0.00%) show no association between Zero and the observed preservation boundary, refuting the original suspicion that Zero -> preservation boundary; concludes Zero should not be treated as the fundamental preservation criterion but as one possible mechanism within a broader architecture that separately includes eliminability/Zero, preservation/adequacy, realization, and reduction cost.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SOURCE -> Transformation / Representation / Inquiry Q / Preservation contract Pi / Decoder O -> Recoverability/Adequacy -> Preservation boundary -> Eliminability(Zero) / Reduction measures
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a revised overall theory architecture diagram superseding the prior linear trajectory (Vedic transformations -> Zero/eliminability -> relationality -> representation reduction -> preservation): SOURCE branches into Transformation, Representation, Inquiry Q, Preservation contract Pi, and Decoder O, which jointly determine Recoverability/Adequacy, which locates a Preservation boundary, which in turn splits into Eliminability (Zero) and Reduction measures as two downstream, non-foundational consequences.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A. Mathematical theory: H(Q|R)=0 ... H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q) ... R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n) => H(Q|R_{n-1}) >= H(Q|R_n). B. KR-ZERO empirical evidence [list]. C. KR-REP-REDUCTION empirical evidence [list].
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the current state of knowledge into three tiers: (A) the mathematical theory -- H(Q|R)=0 as the sufficiency/adequacy criterion, the decomposition H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q) for adequate deterministic representations, and the monotonicity consequence H(Q|R_{n-1})>=H(Q|R_n); (B) a nine-point list of KR-ZERO empirical findings (Zero is context/transformation/contract-relative, group Zero can differ from member Zero, higher-order determination exists but is not universal, interaction order is not globally monotonic, the phenomenon is transformation-dependent, Zero gives no simple universal kernel/algebra); (C) a ten-point list of KR-REP-REDUCTION empirical findings (observable preservation boundary in a sequential chain, boundary detectable via Q-recoverability, first loss at T4 in this run, reduction is multidimensional, adequacy and realization can diverge, a purely representational recoding can leave recoverability unchanged while altering a fixed decoder, Zero did not correlate with the boundary, contract failure and operator-only failure did not occur, non-monotone adequacy was structurally impossible for this chain).

b_rows_sample.anchor: At which transformation does the representation cease to preserve the inquiry we care about? ... Given inquiry Q and preservation contract Pi, does representation R still contain enough information to recover Q? ... a potentially powerful foundation for a KnowledgeOS extraction engine.
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames the practical KnowledgeOS payoff of the representation-reduction results: given a progressive construction chain from raw document through structured representation, claims, relations, normalized claims, knowledge representation, to compressed knowledge representation, the rigorous question 'at which transformation does the representation cease to preserve inquiry Q' can be answered by measuring H(Q|R_n), N_viol(R_n), H(R_n|Q), and representation cost -- proposed as a more rigorous foundation for a KnowledgeOS extraction engine than an informal judgment that summarized information 'still looks present'.

b_rows_sample.statement: States explicitly that the current results do not amount to a general knowledge-extraction theory: they were tested only on a small numerical carrier r=(value, source, timestamp) with a specific Q=(argmax_source, decile(total)) and one particular transformation chain, and transferring the theory to richer carriers (documents, claims, entities, relations, provenance, contradictions, temporal states, evidence) remains an open research question, characterized as 'perfectly fine' rather than a defect.

b_rows_sample.statement: Issues an overall verdict: keep/freeze the old KR-ZERO result (with mechanistic wording narrowed) whose major contribution is that eliminability can be relational, contextual, transformation-dependent, and sometimes higher-order; accept the new KR-REP-REDUCTION result as a successful first representation-reduction experiment whose major contributions are that a specified representation chain can be experimentally tested for preservation with a boundary located without assuming it in advance, that adequacy (what a representation makes recoverable) is distinct from realization (what a particular decoder actually recovers), and that sequential reduction and parallel representation comparison are different mathematical regimes that should become a permanent theoretical distinction.

b_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens the KR-REP-REDUCTION-2026-09 headline claim: the key result is not yet 'representation reduction' but more precisely that the experiment demonstrates contract-relative recoverability loss under a deterministic sequential representation chain D->R5->R4->R3->R2, with the preservation-boundary claim properly restricted to the specified carrier, inquiry, contract, transformation chain, and value alphabet.

b_rows_sample.statement: Re-derives from R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n) with deterministic T_n that H(Q|R_{n-1})>=H(Q|R_n), boxing the consequence 'once sufficiency is lost in this chain, it cannot be recovered downstream', and formally classifies this as '[THEORY] Sequential data-processing constraint' with the accompanying '[NEG] H-C is structurally inapplicable to deterministic sequential reduction' rather than retaining H-C as an empirical hypothesis for this experiment class.

b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes and endorses permanently preserving the distinction between Sequential Reduction (D->R5->R4->R3->R2, where information sufficiency is monotone by data processing) and Alternative/Parallel Representation Comparison (D branching into R_A, R_B, R_C with no data-processing ordering between them, so H(Q|R_A)<H(Q|R_B) is perfectly possible), naming these two distinct research regimes.

b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a three-way conceptual distinction -- Representation (what is encoded), Recoverability (what can in principle be reconstructed), and Realization (what a particular decoder actually reconstructs) -- as strictly non-identical properties, proposed to become a major concept in the future KnowledgeOS extraction architecture, sharper than a mere two-way adequacy-vs-realization split.

b_rows_sample.statement: Requires that the ascending/descending rank representations only be called equivalent (R_up cong_enc R_down) once the implementation demonstrates an actual bijection f,g between them satisfying g.f=id and f.g=id, and that any residual measured difference in H(Q|R) absent such a bijection be attributed to sampling/estimation or implementation effects rather than treated as evidence of non-equivalence; only a confirmed bijection should connect this result to the existing Q-equivalence research.

b_rows_sample.statement: Argues that the negative finding Zero != definition of preservation (observed Zero rates 3.77%, 4.26%, 0% showing no demonstrated correspondence with the R5->R4 preservation boundary) is good news because it prevents the KnowledgeOS theory from becoming circular (Zero -> something can be removed -> therefore preservation), providing evidence that Zero, preservation, realization, and reduction are separate research concerns.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R1 -- non-identifiability is NOT a field... R2 -- structural equality is insufficient... R3 -- the status type is mine, not the corpus's.
a_rows_sample.statement: Three of the ten attacks refute the original proposal: R1, non-identifiability must be a relation over (K1,K2,H,Q) -- two states observationally equivalent under an observation map -- not a label-valued attribute of one item; R2, structural equality is insufficient, shown by an executed counterexample where identical knowledge re-ingested under a new evidence id (E-001 -> E-001-dup) is structurally unequal, so equality must be a FAMILY of relations, not one; R3, the STATUS_VOCAB type is the verifier's own invention -- the corpus has eleven competing vocabularies and designates none, so status is UNDERDETERMINED BY CORPUS.

a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a repaired, fully executable knowledge-state kernel: Item=(q,s,e,c,t,u) with K=FrozenSet[Item]; an equality FAMILY of three distinct relations (eq_struct: literal equality; eq_sem: equality ignoring evidence ids/uncertainty width; eq_obs: equality relative to an explicit observation map H); non-identifiability as the relation H(K1)=H(K2) AND Q(K1)!=Q(K2); and a total, decidable governance predicate G(input,K,ctx,auth,pol) in {0,1}. Every symbol has an explicit value -- no placeholders or oracles.

type_signature.domain: Item tuple, K, observation map H, distinguishing map Q

a_rows_sample.anchor: K0 = {...} ... G(...) = 1 (admissible) ... K1 = {...} ... provenance = {...} ... equality family: structural=False semantic=False observational=True ... nonidentifiable(K0,K1,H,Q) = True ... RESULT: transition COMPUTED. |K0|=1 -> |K1|=2
a_rows_sample.statement: Executes and reports verbatim a concrete state transition: K0 contains one Supported item (Nexus version 3.69); an Add of version 3.70 with new evidence, under policy P-infra-v1 and architect authority in context infra, is admissible (G=1); K1 results with two items (3.69 superseded, valid_to closed; 3.70 added) plus a generated provenance record; the three equality relations disagree on the pair (structural=False, semantic=False, observational=True) and nonidentifiable(K0,K1,H,Q)=True (H cannot distinguish them, Q can). Establishes the transition is computable end to end with authority/policy/evidence/context as decidable guards, provenance generated by the transition rather than stored ad hoc, and non-identifiability computable in practice.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Real artifact read from disk: GovernanceLineageNode ... GovernanceLineageEdge ... Theory requires 5 edge attributes; the implementation supplies 1 fully.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reads real production PHP classes (GovernanceLineageNode: decisionId, integrityHash, decidedAt; GovernanceLineageEdge: fromNodeId, toNodeId, edgeReason) and compares them against the theory's required lineage edge e=(T,A,E,C,tau) (Step 230.13): T(transformation) maps to edgeReason as a bare string; A(authority), E(evidence), C(context) are ABSENT from the implementation; tau(time) exists but on the node, not the edge. Concludes the theory requires 5 edge attributes and the implementation fully supplies only 1.

a_rows_sample.anchor: integrityHash -- cryptographic integrity -- has NO SLOT in the theory's lineage tuple (Step 230.12's {(K_i,T_i,A_i,E_i,tau_i,C_i)}). The theory's lineage edge and the implemented lineage edge DIVERGE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Neither is a superset of the other.
a_rows_sample.statement: The real implementation's integrityHash (cryptographic integrity) has no corresponding slot in the theory's Step-230.12 lineage tuple {(K_i,T_i,A_i,E_i,tau_i,C_i)}; combined with the prior comparison this establishes the theory's edge and the implemented edge diverge in both directions, neither a superset of the other.

a_rows_sample.anchor: my own model is refuted by the real artifact ... decisionId: NO IDENTITY FIELD in my tuple ... integrityHash: NO INTEGRITY FIELD in my tuple ... My proposed K cannot represent a real node either.
a_rows_sample.statement: Tests the verifier's own repaired Item tuple (q,s,e,c,t,u) against the real GovernanceLineageNode fields: decisionId has no matching identity field, integrityHash has no matching integrity field, and decidedAt only partially maps to t.known_from (a single timestamp vs. the tuple's bitemporal design). Records this as a refutation of the verifier's own proposal by running code -- characterized as the strongest available class of evidence against it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: BLOCKER 1 -- ITEM IDENTITY ... Identity is upstream of equality, and equality is upstream of four of the nine operations. The implementation already solves this: decisionId. The theory is behind its own code.
a_rows_sample.statement: Ranks item identity as the highest-leverage blocker: no K-candidate in the corpus (nor the verifier's own proposal) carries an item identity field, without which 'the same item at a later time' is inexpressible, which supersession, replay, merge and deduplication (four of nine operations) all require; identity is upstream of equality. Notes the running implementation already solves this via decisionId -- the theory is behind its own code.

a_rows_sample.anchor: BLOCKER 2 -- EPISTEMIC-STATUS VOCABULARY ... Eleven competing vocabularies; none designated. UNDERDETERMINED BY CORPUS. This is a normative/domain decision, not a mathematical one -- a declared STOP condition. I will not choose it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Declares the epistemic-status vocabulary blocker a normative/domain decision (eleven competing vocabularies exist in the corpus, none designated) rather than a mathematical one, and explicitly refuses to choose on the verifier's own authority -- a declared STOP condition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: BLOCKER 3 -- INTEGRITY ... absent from every late kernel. Step 230-232 dropped a concept the corpus had already built and the code already uses. ... BLOCKER 5 -- TRANSITION AT SCALE ... unmeasured.
a_rows_sample.statement: Blocker 3: integrityHash exists in production code and in Step 073's cryptographic-provenance work but is absent from every late-stage (Step 230-232) kernel formulation -- a concept the corpus had already built and the code already uses was dropped. Blocker 5: the kernel only computes on 1-2 items; complexity/behavior at realistic scale is unmeasured. Also notes the ~25 registries, the four E-scales, and the two kernel lineages are NOT theory gaps but documentation/naming issues -- the underlying mathematics is unaffected by how many times it was renamed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F. Is the theory empirically validated against KnowledgeOS? -- PARTIAL. Confirmed by execution: a typed provenance graph exists, with branching, 47 tests passing. Refuted by execution: the theory's edge tuple != the implemented edge, in both directions. Untested: everything else.
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs a lettered decision tree (A-J): (A) mathematical theory NOT complete (K undefined in corpus, identity/integrity absent, status underdetermined); (B) central knowledge-state object NOT formally defined in the corpus, only in the verifier's own proposal, itself refuted on identity/integrity; (C) computable YES under conditions (designated status vocabulary, identity field, integrity field); (D) at least one real state instantiated YES (K0); (E) at least one real transformation executed YES (T(K0,Add(3.70),...)->K1 with provenance); (F) empirical validation against KnowledgeOS PARTIAL -- confirmed by execution: a typed provenance graph exists with branching and 47 passing tests; refuted by execution: the theory's edge tuple does not equal the implemented edge, in both directions; everything else untested; (G) DDD Ubiquitous Language NOT stable (eleven status vocabularies, four E-scales, ~25 registries, zero crosswalks); (H) architecture PARTIALLY derivable (provenance graph, bitemporal validity, transition-with-guards, Validation->Assessment derivable; anything requiring K/identity/equality not derivable); (I) smallest remaining blocker = ITEM IDENTITY, already answered by decisionId in running code; (J) the resolving experiment: extend the tuple to (id,q,s,e,c,t,u,integrity), re-run the kernel, round-trip a real GovernanceLineageNode through it and assert field-for-field equality -- if it round-trips the theory and implementation are the same object with an empirical anchor; if not, the divergent field is the next blocker.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Nothing here relies on Steps 236 or 239 (FEEDBACK-CONTAMINATED). ... Did the corpus improve? Yes ... Did the corpus independently prove the claim? No -- and it is not counted as having done so.
a_rows_sample.statement: States an explicit source-independence discipline: this analysis derives only from Steps 073, 081, 175, 185, 230, 231, 232 and direct reads of production code, deliberately excluding Steps 236 and 239 as feedback-contaminated (they responded to prior audit). Separates two distinct questions kept apart per an earlier protocol section: did the corpus improve (yes, Steps 236/239 revised prior conclusions in response to audit) versus did the corpus independently prove the claim (no) -- the latter is explicitly not counted as demonstrated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What I did NOT do: Did not choose a status vocabulary ... Did not promote my kernel to theory ... Did not merge the two kernel lineages. Did not repair the corpus's K ... Did not call the executable kernel empirical validation of KnowledgeOS
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly scopes the deliverable's limits: did not choose a status vocabulary (declared normative STOP condition); did not promote the executable kernel to theory status (it remains 'VERIFIER PROPOSAL', refuted on two fields); did not merge the two competing kernel lineages; did not repair the corpus's own unconstructible K, only built and reported an alternative; did not characterize the executable kernel as empirical validation of KnowledgeOS itself, only of a model. Ends with an explicit STOP awaiting supervision before an identity/integrity extension.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT proceed as if the proposed repair Item = (id, q, s, e, c, t, u, integrity) is now the theory. It is only a verifier proposal.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly blocks promoting the prior file's proposed repaired Item tuple (id,q,s,e,c,t,u,integrity) to theory status, reasserting it remains only a verifier proposal to be adversarially re-tested against the complete corpus and the real KnowledgeOS implementation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not simply add id. Determine: Where did the need for identity first arise? Trace the evolution ... first problem -> proposed concept -> refinement -> later formulation -> current implementation. Do NOT assume the latest formulation is correct merely because it is newer.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a full historical derivation search across the corpus for every treatment of identity/identifier/decisionId/equality/deduplication/supersession/lineage/replay/merge, to be organized as an explicit chain (first problem -> proposed concept -> refinement -> later formulation -> current implementation), with change-of-meaning over time preserved rather than collapsed, and an explicit refusal to assume recency implies correctness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT assume that the identifier belongs to an Item. Test at least these possibilities: A. identity of a proposition ... H. identity of an occurrence/version. For each, determine: what entity receives the identity; whether identity is persistent; whether identity survives supersession/re-ingestion/
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires testing 8 distinct candidate referents for 'what bears identity' (a proposition, a knowledge item, an evidence assertion, a state element, a decision, a lineage node, an observation, an occurrence/version) against 7 properties each (persistence, survival under supersession/re-ingestion/serialization, semantic-vs-technical nature, and whether distinct IDs can legitimately denote the same knowledge) -- explicitly refusing to assume identity attaches to 'an Item' by default.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Now determine whether the addition of identity changes their definitions [eq_struct, eq_sem, eq_obs]. ... Construct explicit counterexamples showing cases where: IDs equal but content differs; IDs differ but semantic content is equal; structure is equal but observation differs; observation is equal
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires re-deriving the equality family (adding identity equality to eq_struct/eq_sem/eq_obs from the prior file) with four explicit counterexample patterns (equal-IDs-differing-content; differing-IDs-equal-semantics; equal-structure-differing-observation; equal-observation-differing-state) and a matrix mapping each of 9 operations (Add, Update, Supersede, Merge, Replay, Deduplicate, Validate, Query, Compare) to its actually-required equivalence relation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT automatically add integrity to K. Determine what integrity actually is. ... investigate whether h = Hash(Serialize(K)) is preferable to storing h as a primitive component. Do not choose until the derivation and implementation evidence justify it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Blocks automatically adding an integrity field to K; requires first determining integrity's ontological placement by testing whether it is a property of an Item, a serialized representation, a state, a lineage edge, a cryptographic commitment, a property of provenance, or a verification result, and whether it belongs inside K, T, E, A, or lineage, or is better expressed as a derived function h=Hash(Serialize(K)) rather than a stored primitive -- deferring the choice until derivation and implementation evidence justify it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Now perform the experiment proposed in the previous audit. ... Compare field by field. The result must explicitly classify every field: exact correspondence, derived correspondence, lossy correspondence, theory-only, implementation-only, semantic mismatch. ... If round-trip fails, identify the exact
a_rows_sample.statement: Escalates the prior file's proposed single-artifact round-trip into a required multi-artifact protocol: perform implementation->theory->implementation and theory->implementation mappings against at least 3 structurally different real artifacts (a simple lineage node, a transition/supersession node, a node carrying integrity/provenance), classifying every field into one of 6 explicit categories (exact correspondence, derived correspondence, lossy correspondence, theory-only, implementation-only, semantic mismatch), producing an actual executable assertion rather than a compatibility claim, and identifying the exact first divergent field on failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For every component answer: Why does it exist? What problem requires it? ... Can it be removed without breaking a required capability? ... For every proposed component x in K: Calculate/test K_without_x. Then determine which formally defined capabilities fail. ... Do not call a component necessary m
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires a second, more rigorous minimality test on any revised Item type: a 10-question justification checklist per component (existence reason, problem requiring it, corpus derivation, implementation location, computability, serializability, comparability, transition participation, primitive-vs-derived status, and safe removability), plus an explicit K_without_x removal test per component recorded in a Component/Remove-it/Broken-capability/Counterexample/Necessary table, with the rule that usefulness alone never establishes necessity -- only breaking a formally required capability does.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Add, Remove, Revise, Merge, Split, Supersede, Validate, Reject, Transform. ... What invariants survive these operations?
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 232 (tail) asks whether knowledge states form an algebraic structure under nine operations (Add, Remove, Revise, Merge, Split, Supersede, Validate, Reject, Transform), posing Add(K,x)?, Merge(K1,K2)?, Revise(K,x,x')?, Transform(K_A,C_A,C_B)?, and the key question of what invariants survive these operations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathbb K=\{(G,\sigma,\theta,\lambda,\pi)\mid \text{state satisfies the domain invariants}\}. ... (\mathbb K,\mathcal O)
b_rows_sample.statement: The knowledge-state SPACE mathbb K (all admissible states satisfying domain invariants) is distinguished from a particular STATE mathfrak K_t at time t; rather than assuming a classical algebraic structure (ring/field/vector space), the appropriate initial object is a state-transition algebra (mathbb K, mathcal O) where mathcal O is the set of admissible operations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Transformation\neq Validation. Validation:\mathbb K\times X\rightarrow Assessment while Transformation:\mathbb K\times Parameters\rightarrow\mathbb K.
b_rows_sample.statement: State-changing vs state-classifying operations: Transformation != Validation -- Validation: mathbb K x X -> Assessment (may merely produce an assessment) while Transformation: mathbb K x Parameters -> mathbb K (changes the state); validation may subsequently trigger a transition, corresponding to the DDD chain Command->Decision->Event->State, rated a much better model than treating CRUD as the architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Add_x(\mathfrak K) is a partial operation. ... Remove_x:\mathbb K\rightharpoonup\mathbb K. ... Remove(E) may require Reassess(A).
b_rows_sample.statement: Addition Add_x:mathbb K -> mathbb K is a PARTIAL operation, defined only if Invariant(K')=True; Removal Remove_x:mathbb K -|-> mathbb K is likewise partial since an accepted item may depend on the removed one (A-dependsOn->E), so Remove(E) may require Reassess(A).

b_rows_sample.anchor: x_t\xrightarrow{revisedTo}x_{t+1}. Revision=new state+historical relation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Revision must not be modeled as overwriting (x_t <- x_{t+1}, destroying history) but as x_t -revisedTo-> x_{t+1}, giving Revision = new state + historical relation, naturally supporting lineage.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \sigma(x_1)=Superseded and \sigma(x_2)=Accepted. Currentness\neq Truth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Supersession differs from revision: x1 is retained as historical knowledge marked Superseded (sigma(x1)=Superseded) while x2 is Accepted, again demonstrating Currentness != Truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Merge\neq SetUnion. ... Merge(K_1,K_2,C,P) ... compatible, redundant, complementary, contradictory, superseding. ... TextMerge\neq SemanticMerge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Merge is a partial, semantic operation Merge:mathbb K x mathbb K -|-> mathbb K, not naive set union (Merge != SetUnion) since sources may contain contradictory claims; a proper Merge(K1,K2,C,P) classifies relationships as compatible/redundant/complementary/contradictory/superseding -- giving the DDD principle TextMerge != SemanticMerge (a repository-level/Git merge is not necessarily a domain merge).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Split(Merge(K_1,K_2))\neq(K_1,K_2). ... non-invertible knowledge transformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Split:mathbb K -|-> mathbb K x mathbb K is not a true mathematical inverse of Merge -- Split(Merge(K1,K2)) != (K1,K2) in general because merge may introduce derived information, reconciliation decisions, normalization, or conflict resolution -- an example of non-invertible knowledge transformation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: (\mathcal T,\circ) has the structure of a transformation semigroup, assuming closure. ... (\mathcal T,\circ,I) is at least monoid-like. ... We should not claim it yet as a theorem.
b_rows_sample.statement: The set of admissible transformations mathcal T with composition forms a candidate transformation semigroup (mathcal T, o) assuming closure, with an identity transformation I_K(K)=K making (mathcal T,o,I) at least monoid-like -- explicitly not yet claimed as a proven theorem, but architecturally useful for representing pipelines K3=(T3 o T2 o T1)(K0).

b_rows_sample.anchor: T_2\circ T_1 may be mathematically composable but not governance-valid. MathematicalComposition from GovernedComposition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance breaks naive composition: T1 authorized in context C1 composed with T2 (requiring ungranted authority) may be mathematically composable but not governance-valid, requiring MathematicalComposition to be distinguished from GovernedComposition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal T_G\subseteq\mathcal T ... T\in\mathcal T_G only if Authority(T)\land Policy(T)\land RequiredEvidence(T). ... we should not automatically call \mathcal T_G a semigroup.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governed transformations mathcal T_G subseteq mathcal T require Authority(T) and Policy(T) and RequiredEvidence(T); mathcal T_G is NOT necessarily closed under composition (T1,T2 in T_G but T2 o T1 not in T_G if the combined transformation crosses a governance boundary) -- an important mathematical correction against assuming T_G is a semigroup.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G(T,K,C,A,P)\in\{0,1\}. K'=T(K) only if G(T,K,C,A,P)=1. ... Evidence is a condition of admissibility, not merely metadata.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance is formalized as a boolean constraint system G(T,K,C,A,P) in {0,1}: a state transition K'=T(K) is valid only if G(T,K,C,A,P)=1, and separately E(T) |= ReqEvidence(T,P) must hold -- evidence is a condition of admissibility, not merely metadata. Together these give the core transition rule K_{t+1}=T_t(K_t) subject to G(...)=1 and E_t |= ReqEvidence(T_t,P_t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: M_C(\Delta_t)\Rightarrow Governed(T_t). ... U_t=\varnothing. A governed knowledge system may transform information, but material semantic changes may not occur silently.
b_rows_sample.statement: Material-change condition, rated potentially one of the most important invariants in the entire architecture: M_C(Delta_t)=1 (materiality of the diff between K_t and K_{t+1}) implies Governed(T_t); reformulated elegantly as U_t = empty set where U_t is the set of undeclared material changes -- a governed knowledge system may transform information, but material semantic changes may never occur silently.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t\subseteq K_{t+1} ... Clearly not. ... HistoricalKnowledge(K_t)\subseteq HistoricalKnowledge(K_{t+1}). ... HistoricalMonotonicity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge is NOT monotonic (K_t subseteq K_{t+1} fails since knowledge can be corrected/withdrawn/superseded/invalidated), but a weaker HistoricalMonotonicity holds: HistoricalKnowledge(K_t) subseteq HistoricalKnowledge(K_{t+1}) -- the system should not erase the fact that a knowledge state existed, even though Current(K_t) need not be monotonic while History(K_<=t) should normally grow.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not assume KnowledgeOS is a lattice. It may become a partial order over particular classes of knowledge states, but this requires proof.
b_rows_sample.statement: Whether knowledge states form a lattice under an information ordering K1<=K2 (K2 contains at least as much accepted information) is explicitly left open and cautioned against assuming, since contradictions complicate a least-upper-bound K1 join K2; likewise no universal statistical information ordering should be assumed given multiple incompatible candidates (entropy, KL divergence, Fisher information, posterior concentration).

b_rows_sample.anchor: F_Y=F_X\circ T^{-1}. ... Y must remain linked to X. This is exactly what lineage is supposed to preserve.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distributional transformation is a rigorous statistical-layer example of knowledge transformation: for X~F and measurable T, Y=T(X) induces F_Y = F_X o T^-1; when KnowledgeOS derives an engineering indicator Y from observed metric X, Y must remain linked to X via provenance/uncertainty/assumptions -- exactly what lineage is meant to preserve.

b_rows_sample.anchor: q_1,q_2\xrightarrow{f}q. ... Validity(q)=g(Validity(q_1),Validity(q_2),f).
b_rows_sample.statement: Derived knowledge q=f(q1,q2) gives a knowledge derivation graph q1,q2-f->q; dependency preservation proposes Validity(q) = g(Validity(q1),Validity(q2),f) so that invalidating q1 makes q suspect -- a candidate for deterministic validity propagation, illustrated by Requirement->ArchitectureDecision->ImplementationConstraint where superseding the Requirement triggers Supersession->ImpactAnalysis on the ArchitectureDecision, not necessarily invalidation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Impact(q)=Descendants(q). ... Reassessment(Impact(q)). This may become one of the most important practical capabilities of KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge impact propagation: Impact(q) = Descendants(q) in the provenance/semantic graph, so a material change to q triggers Reassessment(Impact(q)) -- rated potentially one of the most important practical capabilities of KnowledgeOS, and making the transformation algebra explicitly dependency-aware: Input+Context+Evidence+Authority+Dependencies -> Output.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Law 1 -- Traceability ... Law 2 -- Governance ... Law 3 -- Evidence ... Law 4 -- Semantic accountability ... Law 5 -- Historical preservation ... Law 6 -- Epistemic separation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate algebraic laws, rated much closer to architectural invariants than the earlier broad principles: L1 Traceability (exists L(T) for every material transformation), L2 Governance (Material(T)=>Authorized(T)), L3 Evidence (RequiredEvidence(T)=>Evidence(T)), L4 Semantic accountability (MaterialSemanticChange(T)=>Declared(T)), L5 Historical preservation (historical state not silently destroyed), L6 Epistemic separation (Status(q) != Content(q)).

b_rows_sample.anchor: All changes require human approval is a policy. It is not necessarily a universal architectural invariant. ... Every consequential transformation requires an authority mechanism appropriate to its risk and policy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Crucial distinction between invariant and policy: 'all changes require human approval' is a policy, not a universal invariant; the more general, robust invariant is 'every consequential transformation requires an authority mechanism appropriate to its risk and policy' (human approval, delegated authority, deterministic policy, or automated rule).

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 's1595-executable-kernel-and-blocker-ranking' POSSIBLY relates to 'step232-knowledge-state-algebra' (batch B0039). Note: A verifier-authored, executed (not merely PASS-labeled) repaired candidate knowledge-state kernel Item=(q,s,e,c,t,u) with an equality-relation family and a decidable governance predicate; runs a real K0->K1 transition with provenance, then empirically tests it against real GovernanceLineageNode/Edge PHP classes, finding mutual divergence; ranks 5 blockers (item identity, status vocabulary, integrity, equality family, scale) and ends STOPPED awaiting supervision. Distinct from but responsive to Steps 230-232's kernel candidates.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What is the smallest formally valid mathematical system that can represent the KnowledgeOS semantics demonstrated by the corpus, without confusing state, evidence, assessment, transformation, governance and history? ... The final result may be: a Knowledge State, a state plus external assessment str
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the central research question around minimality-without-confusion across 6 named categories (state, evidence, assessment, transformation, governance, history) and explicitly enumerates 5 possible final architectural shapes without pre-selecting any of them, forbidding K5/K8 selection as an answer.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Given a concrete candidate K, can Claude actually calculate whether K in K? If not, K is still incompletely defined. ... Construct K_A, K_B [differing in evidence, epistemic qualification, temporal qualification, history]. ... T(K_A,input,context,policy,authority)=K_B ... No placeholders. No 'would'
a_rows_sample.statement: Sets an operational completeness test for the validity predicate (can Claude actually compute K in K for a concrete candidate, not merely assert it), requires constructing two concrete states K_A/K_B differing along 4 axes (evidence, epistemic qualification, temporal qualification, history) rather than one, and requires an actually executed (not simulated or hedged with 'would') concrete transition with named/typed/valued arguments and an explicit precondition check before computing and validating the result.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not force all operations to be transformations K->K. Validation may instead be K x X -> Assessment. Replay may be History x Input -> K. Authority may be Actor x Action x Context -> Authorization. Governance may be Policy x Transformation -> Assessment/Decision. These are hypotheses to test, not c
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the assumption that every theory operation must have the shape K->K, proposing 4 differently-shaped candidate operation signatures (Validation: KxX->Assessment; Replay: History x Input -> K; Authority: Actor x Action x Context -> Authorization; Governance: Policy x Transformation -> Assessment/Decision), explicitly as hypotheses for the ten named operations (Add, Remove, Update, Merge, Supersede, Split, Accept, Reject, Validate, Replay), not settled conclusions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For every major proposed statement use: CLAIM, FORMALIZATION, ASSUMPTIONS, PROOF or COUNTEREXAMPLE, VERDICT. Never write 'therefore' unless the preceding reasoning actually establishes the implication.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a mandatory 5-part theorem/counterexample discipline (CLAIM / FORMALIZATION / ASSUMPTIONS / PROOF-or-COUNTEREXAMPLE / VERDICT) for every major statement in the deliverable, and an explicit ban on the connective 'therefore' unless the preceding reasoning actually establishes the implication -- a rhetorical-rigor constraint not present in the batch's earlier mandates.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Using an actual existing KnowledgeOS/EKS artifact, determine: [10 questions: current state, proposition, observation, evidence, assessment, transformation, policy, authority, lineage, resulting state]. If an actual artifact cannot be represented without inventing fields that do not exist, record tha
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires a 10-question engineering test mapping a real KnowledgeOS/EKS artifact onto the theory's categories (state, proposition, observation, evidence, assessment, transformation, policy, authority, lineage, resulting state), with any invented field recorded as an implementation gap rather than silently patched, and an explicit ban on adjusting the theory to accommodate one artifact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The final theory must emerge from: requirements -> types -> relations -> valid states -> equality -> transformations -> assessments -> history -> invariants -> computability -> engineering validation -- not from choosing an attractive tuple first. Do not proceed to a new kernel label until the mathe
a_rows_sample.statement: States the mandate's governing construction order: a valid theory must be derived through an 11-stage sequence (requirements, types, relations, valid states, equality, transformations, assessments, history, invariants, computability, engineering validation), never by selecting an attractive kernel tuple first and working backward -- and explicitly forbids introducing any new kernel label before that sequence is honored.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Only one genuine conflict: policy placement. ... Classification: GENUINE CONTRADICTION between the prior audits and Step 245 on pi. ... Feedback-loop check: Step 245 fingerprinted against all verifier artifacts -- (q,s,e,c,t,u) 0 hits ... Classification: SOURCE-INDEPENDENT.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executes the mandated 10-row reconciliation table, finding only one genuine contradiction (policy pi's placement, Step 245 inside K vs prior audits outside) with everything else being unaddressed-but-not-contradictory; runs a feedback-loop fingerprint check (searching Step 245 for verifier-specific terminology, 0 hits) and classifies Step 245 as SOURCE-INDEPENDENT evidence, continuing Step 232's own inner tuple rather than responding to this verification programme.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Model B executed -- K=(C,sigma,theta,lambda) with policy as an argument to T ... If pi in K, then revoking or amending a policy changes every stored state, while nothing that is known has changed. ... VERDICT: pi is EXTERNAL. MATHEMATICALLY VERIFIED by counterexample.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executes Model B (policy external to K, passed as an argument to T) successfully, and gives a counterexample against Model A (policy internal): if pi were in K, revoking/amending a policy would change every stored state despite no change in what is known, and two states holding identical knowledge under different policies would be unequal -- policy governs the transition, not what is known. Verdict: pi is external to K, mathematically verified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: same proposition, different evidence: Observed vs Supported ... same proposition+evidence, different policy: Observed vs Unknown ... Model 1 REFUTED ... Model 2 REFUTED (insufficient) ... Model 3 SURVIVES ... sigma is not a primitive of the Knowledge State. It is derived from an Assessment.
a_rows_sample.statement: Tests all three S1602-mandated sigma models by execution: Model 1 (sigma:Proposition->Status) is refuted because one proposition yields three distinct status values depending on context; Model 2 (adding Evidence,Context) is refuted as insufficient because policy also changes the outcome and is not an argument; Model 3 (a full Assessment function over Proposition,Evidence,Context,Policy, with Status derived) survives. Concludes epistemic status is a derived Assessment output, not a Knowledge-State primitive -- noted as exactly Step 232.4's Validation:K x X->Assessment shape, extended to status, which Step 245 had re-internalized as a primitive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the same proposition Nexus.version=3.69 carries two assertion instances: assert-1 valid 2026-01-01..2026-06-01; assert-2 valid 2026-03-01..infinity. A function theta: Proposition -> Interval cannot return two values for one input. VERDICT: temporal validity belongs to the ASSERTION instance, not the
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a direct counterexample refuting theta as a function of Proposition alone: the same proposition can carry two overlapping-but-distinct assertion instances with different validity intervals, which a single-valued function theta:Proposition->Interval cannot represent. Verdict: temporal validity belongs to the assertion instance, mathematically verified; also notes the four bitemporal dimensions (valid/known/record/decision time) are not collapsible to one timestamp, yet the real implementation does collapse them to a single decidedAt field -- flagged as an IMPLEMENTATION GAP.

b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms Transform need not be unary (T:KxQxC->K', a typed state transition rather than a closed K->K function), reaffirms that every semantically relevant external dependency (policy, time, authority, evidence) must be an explicit argument to preserve determinism, and proposes an unestablished provenance-propagation model Prov(k')=Prov(k) union Prov(q) union Prov(c) for Transform specifically.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If k enters the system with Prov(k)=p0, then History(T_0)=empty while Prov(k)=p0. Thus the earlier counterexample survives.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reconfirms the Step 254 (S1620) provenance-at-t=0 base-case counterexample using the Transform operation's own provenance-propagation model, showing it independently survives when applied specifically to Transform.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Supersede => Identity, but does not establish Identity subseteq K until we know whether identity is represented in the state or externally resolvable. ... Temporal order != Supersession relation. ... A provenance-preserving model may require Prov(x2) superset-or-equal Prov(x1). But perhaps the super
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes 3 findings for Supersede: it requires stable identity for both operands (Supersede implies Identity, without settling whether identity lives in K); temporal event-ordering (t1<t2) must not be conflated with semantic supersession precedence (x2 succ x1) -- they are logically independent; and provenance propagation under supersession cannot be assumed equal between old and new, requiring an explicit rule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H1: x0->x1 with x1 succ x0. H2: x1. If SupersessionHistory(x1) is semantically observable, then H1 and H2 cannot be collapsed. If no mandatory operation observes supersession history, then the histories may be equivalent. Therefore this is a conditional counterexample.
b_rows_sample.statement: Constructs a conditional (not established) counterexample for Supersede: whether two histories differing only in supersession lineage but sharing the same current object must be distinguished depends entirely on whether any mandatory operation actually observes supersession history.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Three possible Merge identity semantics: New identity id(x3)!=id(x1),id(x2); One-source identity retained id(x3)=id(x1); Composite identity id(x3)=f(id(x1),id(x2)). The corpus does not establish which model is correct. Merge cannot be fully typed until identity semantics are fixed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses 3 mutually exclusive identity semantics for the result of Merge (entirely new identity, one source's identity retained, or a composite function of both sources' identities), none established by the corpus, concluding Merge cannot be fully typed until this is resolved.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Prov(x3) superset-or-equal Prov(x1) union Prov(x2). If that invariant is mandatory, then Merge is provenance-sensitive. ... This experiment therefore directly tests the architectural placement of provenance. ... Merge requires a semantic preservation invariant [Meaning(x3) must relate appropriately
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies Merge as the strongest available operational test for provenance placement: if a mandatory provenance-union invariant holds, Merge is provenance-sensitive and this experiment directly tests where provenance architecturally belongs; separately notes Merge requires an unspecified, domain-specific semantic-preservation invariant relating the merged meaning to its sources' meanings.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The four operations do not require identical semantic inputs. Therefore a single universal signature T:KxP->K is likely too coarse. Instead T = {T1,...,Tn} should be treated as a typed family. ... Operation dependency != State membership. Transform(K,Policy) does not imply Policy subseteq K. Similar
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms via the 4-operation dependency comparison that a single universal transformation signature is too coarse (the operations need different inputs), reinforcing the typed-family conclusion, and restates the operation-dependency != state-membership principle with concrete Transform/Policy and Merge/Evidence examples.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The strongest dependencies are currently: Supersede => Identity, Revise => Identity, Merge => Identity, and potentially Merge => Provenance. ... This means identity may be a more fundamental candidate for K than some of the earlier kernel components. But that remains a candidate, not a conclusion.
b_rows_sample.statement: Aggregates the per-operation dependency findings, showing Identity is required by 3 of the 4 discriminating operations (Supersede, Revise, Merge) and Provenance potentially by a 4th aspect (Merge), tentatively elevating Identity to a more fundamental kernel candidate than some earlier components -- explicitly flagged as a candidate, not a proven conclusion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We previously treated Equality_K as foundational. But operationally, Identity must first be distinguished from Equality. Two states can be equal while containing different historical identities, depending on the chosen equivalence. Identity != Equality. The theory needs both concepts, even if they e
b_rows_sample.statement: States the step's fourth major finding, reordering the theory's foundational priorities: Identity must be distinguished from Equality operationally, contrary to earlier treatment of Equality_K as the sole foundational relation -- two states can be equal under a chosen equivalence while containing different historical identities, so both concepts are independently needed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: id(x1)=id(x2) does not necessarily imply x1=x2 as values. Likewise x1=x2 under extensional equality does not necessarily tell us whether they arose from the same lineage. This distinction will become critical in Step 258.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives the formal separation between identity persistence (id(x1)=id(x2)) and value/extensional equality (x1=x2): neither implies the other, since identical identity does not guarantee identical current values, and extensional equality does not reveal shared lineage.

b_rows_sample.anchor: History dependence of implementation != History dependence of state semantics. ... The operation might internally inspect history while still producing the same semantically relevant state. ... Only the second disproves state sufficiency.
b_rows_sample.statement: Draws a critical architectural distinction between an operation's implementation inspecting history internally (That(H1)!=That(H2)) versus history actually affecting the resulting semantic state (F(That(H1))!=F(That(H2))) -- only the latter disproves state sufficiency; an operation may legitimately look at history while still producing an observably identical state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the provenance base-case counterexample alone does not establish that provenance belongs in K. It establishes only that provenance cannot be reconstructed from transformation history alone. ... External provenance is information-theoretically irreducible from T-history, but it is not yet proven sema
b_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens the recurring provenance conclusion into its most defensible final form, explicitly proposed as a permanent theory distinction: external provenance is information-theoretically irreducible from transformation history (proven), but this does NOT prove provenance is semantically constitutive of the Knowledge State itself (not proven) -- it may remain purely audit/lineage information without being part of K's identity/equality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Revise: identity + provenance semantics unresolved (yellow). Transform: exact context signature unresolved (yellow/green). Supersede: identity + temporal/provenance semantics unresolved (yellow). Merge: identity + preservation/provenance unresolved (yellow). These are now sufficiently structured to
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the post-Step-257 formalization status of all 4 discriminating operations, each still carrying unresolved identity and/or provenance dependencies but now sufficiently structured to serve as concrete experimental test cases for the congruence criterion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The next step should therefore isolate the issue that all four operations depend upon: Identity and Equality. ... Step 258 -- Identity, Equality and Knowledge-State Equivalence. When are two Knowledge Objects the same? and separately: When are two Knowledge States equivalent? These must not be confl
b_rows_sample.statement: Sets Step 258 to isolate Identity and Equality as the common dependency of all 4 discriminating operations, requiring 3 explicitly distinct relations (object equality =_X, Knowledge-State equivalence equiv_K, history equivalence cong_H, never conflated) and a congruence requirement (equiv_K preserved by every mandatory transformation) as the decisive criterion for whether a proposed equivalence is a legitimate semantic quotient.

b_rows_sample.anchor: =_I cannot by itself be the semantic equality relation [fails Revise, which requires semantic change while identity persists]. ... Content equality cannot replace identity [fails Merge/Supersede, which must distinguish independently-created identical-content objects].
b_rows_sample.statement: Proves both identity-only equality and content-only equality are individually insufficient as the semantic equality relation: identity-only equality cannot represent Revise (which needs semantic change while identity persists); content-only equality cannot represent Merge/Supersede (which must distinguish two independently-created objects with identical content).

b_rows_sample.anchor: For a composition operation Merge(K1,K2) to be well-defined, the result must be independent of representatives. ... This is exactly another congruence requirement. Composability is not automatic from quotient existence. ... If Merge(H1,H2) not-equiv Merge(H1',H2'), then Merge does not descend to the
b_rows_sample.statement: Proves Composability of Merge over the quotient is a distinct congruence requirement (representative-independence: equivalent inputs must produce equivalent Merge outputs), not automatic from mere quotient existence; if it fails, Merge simply does not descend to a well-defined K* x K* -> K* operation, requiring one of 5 named remedies (a richer K, additional external context, a restricted Merge domain, a partial operation, or a different semantic interpretation).

b_rows_sample.statement: Information-Timeliness Principle: control/decision performance depends on when information becomes available, not merely on whether it exists; delayed measurements degrade performance.
