b_rows_sample.statement: The book's page-8 observation->estimator->feedback diagram is cited as primary visual evidence supporting a proposed closed-loop KnowledgeOS research hypothesis chain, making the state estimate an explicit intermediate object between raw evidence and decision, contrasted with a bare prompt->LLM->answer model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the stochastic state models explicitly carry both mean and covariance ... uncertainty should not necessarily be treated as metadata attached after the fact.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uncertainty (mean and covariance) is carried as an intrinsic part of the state model itself, not attached as after-the-fact metadata to a point estimate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: convergence with probability one, convergence in probability, and mean-square convergence ... 'stable,' 'converged,' 'repeatable,' and 'assured' should not be collapsed into one concept.
b_rows_sample.statement: Multiple distinct convergence notions (probability-one, in-probability, mean-square) mapped onto a caution that KnowledgeOS assurance vocabulary terms (stable/converged/repeatable/assured) must remain distinct rather than collapsing into one concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Astrom imposes regularity conditions such as finite variance and continuity assumptions. ... a very strong Zero Lens candidate: what conditions must hold before a model or inference is even legitimate?
b_rows_sample.statement: Model-validity regularity conditions (finite variance, continuity) before a stochastic differential equation is meaningful, offered as a strong Zero-Lens candidate for KnowledgeOS model-legitimacy prerequisites.

b_rows_sample.anchor: an integral can exist even when the underlying dynamic system is unstable. ... a measurable/finite result does not necessarily imply a valid or stable system.
b_rows_sample.statement: Stability-vs-finite-result warning: a finite/measurable computed quantity (e.g. an integral) can exist even when the underlying system is unstable, important for deterministic assurance (a passing metric does not imply a valid or stable system).

b_rows_sample.anchor: this particular uploaded volume is much more foundational than its title might suggest ... does not appear to contain a large modern treatment of Kalman filtering or dynamic programming. ... I would not import concepts such as 'Kalman filter' or 'dynamic programming' into the extraction as though they were developed by this source.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit source-fidelity correction: despite the topic area, this specific 150-page scanned volume does not itself develop a full modern Kalman-filter or dynamic-programming treatment, so those concepts must not be attributed to this source in the extraction record.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What does it mean to maintain a sufficient, uncertainty-aware state of knowledge from which a governed engineering decision can be made? That is potentially more fundamental to KnowledgeOS than any individual stochastic-control algorithm.
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames the book's deepest contribution as a research question (maintaining a sufficient, uncertainty-aware knowledge state for governed decisions) rather than any specific control algorithm, and provides a classification table (Sufficient State, Information Timeliness, State Estimation, Observation-vs-Estimated-State, Uncertainty-as-State-Property, Markov/Sufficient-History rated Very-High/INVESTIGATE; Convergence Taxonomy and Model Preconditions rated High/ADAPT; Spectral Factorization Medium; Stochastic Calculus and polynomial/numerical optimization machinery Low/RECORD ONLY).

b_rows_sample.anchor: uncertain environment → observation → sufficient state → estimation → decision → action → new observation ... What does it mean to maintain a sufficient, uncertainty-aware state of knowledge from which a governed engineering decision can be made?
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces 'sufficient state' (Astrom's control-theory loop: uncertain environment -> observation -> sufficient state -> estimation -> decision -> action -> new observation) as the most operational temporal concept in the corpus: a retention criterion asking what minimum must be retained so a governed decision remains possible, distinct from what-changes/what-persists/what-absence-means questions elsewhere in the temporal family; gives a principled answer-shape to S1-F001's measured-but-unanswerable question of whether authority was valid at a past point in time.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Retaining every prior state of the aggregate therefore does not retain the grant's validity interval, because the interval was never inside the aggregate to be retained.
b_rows_sample.statement: Sufficient state (Astrom) gives a principled answer shape to a previously-measured gap: was a given authority grant valid at a particular historical point in time? Forward-only history retains every prior state of an aggregate's members, but Authority is held by the Authority context and only referenced by the aggregate (a Reference, l.211), so retaining the aggregate's prior states does not retain the grant's own validity interval -- the interval was never inside the aggregate to retain. Sufficient state and the earlier measured gap are the same hole from opposite ends: one asks what must be retained for the question to be answerable, the other measured that it isn't answerable. This does not change the earlier IMPLEMENTATION QUESTION verdict (the Authority context may hold the interval, uninspectable here), but names the sufficiency criterion precisely.

b_rows_sample.anchor: They are not independent. Freedman is statistical decision theory; Åström is stochastic control. **Both fields define adequacy relative to a decision by construction**
b_rows_sample.statement: Session 1 read S1-F029's abstention threshold (a sufficiently safe decision) and S1-F034's sufficient state (from which a governed decision can be made) as two independent arrivals at 'adequacy is relative to use'. This review disputes independence: Freedman's sufficient statistic and Astrom's sufficient state are the same technical move in adjacent disciplines (statistical decision theory and stochastic control), both defining adequacy relative to a decision by construction -- so the convergence is a property of the source fields being drawn from, not independent evidence about KnowledgeOS. This compounds a related finding (S2-R-F029.3): decision-relative adequacy requires the boundary to know what decision the knowledge will inform, while 'workflow' and 'decision' sit on exclusion/not-own lists elsewhere (S1-F011, F009, F019) -- two sources now pull toward decision-relativity while three formulations exclude decisions, and the two pulling sources share a disciplinary prior that makes their pull unsurprising.

b_rows_sample.anchor: "Topology is our analytical lens; it is not presented by Åström as the organizing theory of the book."
b_rows_sample.statement: Session 1 explicitly disclaims that topology is the reviewers' own analytical lens applied to Astrom's material, not something Astrom himself presents as the book's organizing theory -- a cheap, repeatable one-line lens-honesty discipline the reviewer says is exactly what the Zero-lens provenance mess (X-005) shows this corpus needed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **Convergence note:** two routes to one hole — `S1-F001` measured that the question is unanswerable; `S1-F034` states what would make it answerable.
b_rows_sample.statement: A 2026-08-28 update: S1-F034's 'sufficient state' (the minimum that must be retained so a governed decision remains possible) supplies the missing criterion for this finding, without changing its verdict. Retaining every prior state of an aggregate's members (forward-only history) does not retain a grant's validity interval, since Authority is a Reference held by the Authority context, not inside the aggregate -- retention is not sufficiency. Verdict remains IMPLEMENTATION QUESTION; only specificity changes. Recorded as a POSSIBLE INDEPENDENT ARRIVAL at the same hole from two directions, though both reach the reviewer through the same Session-1 extraction, so the extraction step itself is common to them.

b_aliases: sufficient information for future probability distribution

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'state-sufficiency-candidate-definition-285' POSSIBLY relates to 'sufficient-state-control-theory-lens' (batch B0050). Note: Candidate (explicitly not-yet-solved) definition of Sufficient(K,𝒪,ℐ): K is sufficient iff it contains enough information to (1) evaluate every mandatory invariant, (2) determine operation legality, (3) execute every canonical transformation, (4) distinguish required state identities, (5) support required equality decisions, (6) support deterministic replay where required. Paired with an information-theoretic reducibility test: an operation-legality decision L(o,K) must not silently depend on extra information X unless X is declared an explicit external dependency.

a_rows_sample.statement: Tracked as TV-F-083: the corpus repairs its own ill-typed central claim across three stages, unprompted -- Step 215 SS215.10 'SemanticIntegrity proportional-to DistinctionPreservation' (ill-typed, proportional-to demands ratio scales neither side has, hence unfalsifiable) -> Step 219 SS219.25 'SI(K,T)=Preservation(CriticalSemantics(K))' (well-formed definition, not yet falsifiable) -> Step 222 SS222.12 'SI(T,K,C)=1 iff CriticalSemantics(K,C) subseteq Recoverable(T(K)) or Loss(T,K,C) is explicitly represented, else SI=0' (falsifiable, set-theoretic, well-formed; the file itself states 'this gives the concept a falsifiable form'). Neither 219 nor 222 cites or marks 215 SS215.10 superseded, so under LATER!=SUPERSEDING all three forms remain live and are recorded as UNRECONCILED ALTERNATIVES -- only the third is falsifiable. a_rows_sample.anchor: Its epistemic discipline has improved markedly and genuinely ... Its evidential base has not moved at all. It has become rigorous about what it does not know, without yet going to find out.
a_rows_sample.statement: Overall assessment: Step 222 is rated the strongest single file in the last thirty steps and possibly in the corpus -- completing a 3-stage self-repair of SemanticIntegrity into a falsifiable form, introducing conditional invariants dissolving 4/5 documented MCS contradictions, correctly stating the falsifiability criterion, refusing three overclaim opportunities, and independently reaching this programme's contradiction-as-boundary-discovery adjudication, while committing zero measurement-theoretic violations (a first). Yet it tests nothing: its falsification matrix and F(P) computation remain empty. Trajectory verdict over Steps 208-222: epistemic discipline has improved markedly and genuinely (no fabrication, no self-awarded PASS, correct refusals, self-repair of its own defects, a falsifiable central definition) but the evidential base has not moved at all -- rigorous about what it does not know, without yet going to find out.

a_rows_sample.anchor: MCS-1 ... REFINEMENT -- but conditional on an UNDECLARED projection ... MCS-2 ... NOT DISSOLVED -- survives ... MCS-3 ... DISSOLVED -- but by a DIFFERENT mechanism ... MCS-4 ... RELOCATED, not dissolved ... MCS-5 ... DISSOLVED by disambiguation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executed re-test of all 5 minimal conflicting subsets (MCS) against the conditional-invariant repair I_i:C_i=>R_i, per the verification directive's mandated 5-step procedure: MCS-1 (Unknown semantics) -- contexts C_verif/C_display are genuinely mutually exclusive and conditionalization would restore satisfiability, but only if a projection pi:{T,F,U}->{PASS,DEGRADED,FAIL} is declared, which the corpus never does -- rated 'refinement available, not taken'. MCS-2 (Retention) -- satisfiability returns only by asserting KnowableQ (flipping a premise, not scoping a rule; a governance decision no step has made) -- confirmed NOT dissolved, as Step 222 itself reports. MCS-3 (Aggregate ownership) -- Owns and Participates are different RELATIONS, not different contexts, not mutually exclusive and need not be; the conflict is dissolved by splitting the conflated relations, not by Step 222's context-scoping machinery at all. MCS-4 (Epistemic ordering) -- the chain holds only 'on a subdomain where the states are comparable', but which states are comparable is never specified, making mutual exclusivity undecidable -- the contradiction is relocated into an undefined condition, not resolved. MCS-5 (Entropy) -- H denotes two different quantities (conditional entropy vs. entropy of the growing state description) bound to one glyph; genuinely dissolved by disambiguation, though the corpus never states which quantity it means in each expression.

a_rows_sample.anchor: genuinely dissolved by conditionalisation : 2 ... dissolved by a DIFFERENT mechanism : 1 ... relocated into an undefined condition : 1 ... survives : 1
a_rows_sample.statement: Part 2 verdict, explicitly correcting the verifier's own prior record: conditional invariants are a genuine advance over Step 209's flat conjunction, but do NOT dissolve four of five MCS as previously claimed -- the tested breakdown is 2 genuinely dissolved by conditionalization (MCS-1 conditional on an undeclared projection, MCS-5), 1 dissolved by a different mechanism entirely (MCS-3, relation-splitting not context-scoping), 1 relocated into an undefined condition rather than resolved (MCS-4), and 1 survives unresolved (MCS-2) -- every dissolution additionally requires a declaration the corpus has not yet made.

b_rows_sample.statement: Step-029's worked SAT example ((A∨B)∧(¬A∨C)) is verifier-recomputed to have 4 satisfying models, contradicting the source's hedge 'may exist'; the file's 'no SMT solver needed everywhere' decision criterion is asserted with no complexity claim, no cost model, and no classification procedure for 'simple' vs solver-requiring constraints, while its own companion meta file lists complexity analysis as 'Not yet analyzed'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #1 — Knowledge as a generic object: forbidden in 208, used as an Owner in 210
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.28 boxes a prohibition: the Data->Information->Evidence->Assessment->KnowledgeClaim transformations of semantic status 'should not [be collapsed] into one generic object called Knowledge.' Step 210 Section 210.25's matrix row I11 nonetheless assigns Owner='Knowledge' (and row I3 compounds it with 'Knowledge infrastructure'), the exact generic object Step 208 boxed a prohibition against two files earlier in the same band. Severity HIGH; neither Step-206 bounded context, and neither file notices.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #3 — The evidence-strength scale is recalibrated between Step 210 and Step 212
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.30 defines E_1=documentation, E_2=manual inspection, E_3=automated test, E_4=property-based test, E_5=formal verification. Step 212 Section 212.6 defines E_0=No evidence, E_1=Claim/documentation, E_2=Static implementation evidence, E_3=Executable test evidence, E_4=Runtime/production evidence, E_5=Formal verification. E_2, E_3 and E_4 disagree between the two files (only E_5 agrees), so a claim 'has E_4 evidence' means a property-based test under Step 210 and production observation under Step 212 -- entirely different assurance. Aggravating factor: Step 212's calibration silently matches the uncited Step 109's (E2=implementation, E4=runtime), so Step 212 restores an earlier convention without knowing it. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #4 — E_1 bound twice inside Step 210 itself
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.20 writes E_1⇒P and E_2⇒¬P (evidence items entailing propositions); Step 210 Section 210.30, ten sections later, writes E_1=documentation (an ordinal assurance rung). Same symbol, same document, incompatible types, undisambiguated. Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #5 — Evidence/Test ordering reversed between Step 210's own boxed conclusion and Step 211's boxed conclusion
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.40 boxes Invariant->Owner->Enforcement->Evidence->Test->Assurance; Step 211 Section 211.2 boxes I->Owner->Mechanism->Test->Evidence -- directly conflicting orderings, both boxed as conclusions in consecutive files. Step 210's own Section 210.1 tuple and Step 209's tail agenda both side with Step 211's ordering, so Step 210's boxed conclusion contradicts Step 210's own boxed tuple. Severity MEDIUM; the direction matters since Evidence->Test means evidence licenses the test while Test->Evidence means the test produces the evidence, which is what Steps 212-214 assume throughout.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #6 — min over assurance vs. the prohibition on scalarization, both boxed in Step 211
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 211 Section 211.6 states Assurance(I_global)<=min{Assurance(I_1),Assurance(I_2),...}; Step 211 Section 211.17 boxes 'Vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization.' min over a set requires a total order on the codomain, but Section 211.9 makes assurance a 6-vector (only partially ordered), so evaluating min requires exactly the scalarization Section 211.17 forbids -- the two boxed positions of one file are mutually exclusive. Aggravated by Section 211.4's ordinal-only assurance-adjacent quantities and by Section 211.17's own use of cardinal values A_s=1, A_p=0, 0.83. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #7 — Step 212 builds ownership diagnostics and deletes the ownership data needed to run them

a_rows_sample.statement: Step 213 Section 213.26 mandates that every important statement during reconstruction carry an [F]/[D]/[P]/[U] label ('our editorial control system'). b_rows_sample.anchor: What happened? ... What remained unknown? ... R(S_i)=(O_i,L_i,A_i,V_i,U_i)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-question per-step reconstruction record R(S_i)=(Observation,Learning,Architecture,Verification,Unknown) to be applied to each of Steps 1-182, explicitly changing mode from generating new theory to reconstructing the evidentiary basis of existing theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: StepCount ≠ KnowledgeCount ... exploratory; repetitive; corrective; validation; implementation; philosophical; mathematical; editorial; prompt-engineering; synthesis
b_rows_sample.statement: States that a conversational 'step' is not necessarily an architectural contribution (some are exploratory, repetitive, corrective, editorial, etc.), so StepCount != KnowledgeCount, requiring the reconstruction to discover the actual knowledge-bearing events rather than treat all 182 steps as equal.

b_rows_sample.anchor: OBS Observation ... UNK Insufficient evidence ... A single step can have more than one tag internally
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a 14-code step-type classification (OBS/EXP/MAT/DDD/ARC/GOV/AI/VER/FAIL/DEC/PHI/SYN/REP/UNK) allowing multiple tags per step, crossed with the F/D/P/U epistemic-status axis (Type x EpistemicStatus) so e.g. 'ARC+D' denotes an architectural derivation rather than an observed fact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Which architectural principles appear independently more than once? ... Convergence(I) = NumberOfIndependentEvidencePaths(I) ... We should not immediately turn this into a numerical quality score
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a convergence test: if the same architectural principle emerges from multiple unrelated observations (P_1, P_7, P_31 all pointing to invariant I), that repeated independent emergence is treated as strong evidence the principle is fundamental, formalized as Convergence(I)=NumberOfIndependentEvidencePaths(I) but explicitly not reduced to a numerical quality score.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity≠State ... Knowledge≠Authority ... Unknown≠False ... CurrentState≠History ... Generation≠Validation ... Validation≠Authorization ... Claim→Evidence ... Context_A≠Context_B ... These are candidate principles, not yet declared final conclusions
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists ten candidate recurring architectural distinctions to be tested against the actual Steps-1-182 evidence rather than accepted by default (Identity!=State, Knowledge!=Authority, Decision!=Execution, Execution!=Outcome, Unknown!=False, CurrentState!=History, Generation!=Validation, Validation!=Authorization, Claim->Evidence, Context_A!=Context_B), explicitly labelled candidates pending evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: They are all forms of: A ≠ B where software engineering frequently makes the mistake: A ≈ B ... restoring distinctions that had been collapsed
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a deeper common structure across the recurring principles: each is an instance of A!=B guarding against a common engineering mistake of collapsing A~=B (Identity~=State, Prediction~=Truth, Knowledge~=Authority, Execution~=Outcome), proposing this pattern-of-restoring-collapsed-distinctions as possibly one of the deepest architectural themes in the entire book.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Robust knowledge-centric software depends on preserving distinctions that carry semantic, temporal, epistemic or governance meaning ... SemanticIntegrity ∝ DistinctionPreservation ... a hypothesis, not a proven theorem
b_rows_sample.statement: States the 'distinction preservation' hypothesis (robust knowledge-centric software depends on preserving semantically/temporally/epistemically/governance-meaningful distinctions), formalized as SemanticIntegrity proportional-to DistinctionPreservation, explicitly labelled a hypothesis to be tested against the Steps-1-182 evidence rather than a proven theorem; connects this across DDD (Entity!=ValueObject), mathematics (x!=y), statistics (Observed!=Inferred, Correlation!=Causation), governance (Capability!=Authority) and AI engineering (Generation!=Verification) as convergent instances of one meta-principle: do not collapse distinctions that matter.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Krishna ~ Perspective possessing continuity across changing manifestations ... What would a software system need if it were required to preserve continuity across changing states? ... Versioning, Provenance, History, Lineage, Context
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a careful literary (not architectural) interpretation of Krishna as 'a perspective possessing continuity across changing manifestations', translating this into the engineering question of what a system needs to preserve continuity across changing states (versioning, provenance, history, lineage, context), explicitly warning against the trivializing claim 'Krishna is the system's memory'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Philosophical Analogy ≠ Technical Proof ... Outcome A ... retrospective analogy ... Outcome B ... repeatedly influenced ... Outcome C ... independently emerged technically and philosophically ... the most interesting result
b_rows_sample.statement: States three possible historical outcomes for the Gita lens's actual role to be determined by the reconstruction rather than assumed: (A) it was purely a retrospective analogy applied after the fact, (B) it repeatedly and genuinely influenced engineering questions during development, (C) the same principles independently emerged both technically and philosophically -- rated the most interesting possible result, expressible as EngineeringObservation<->PhilosophicalReflection without either proving the other.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose a technical invariant existed before the corresponding Gītā reflection ... TechnicalDiscovery -> PhilosophicalRecognition ... those are different histories. The Evidence Ledger will tell us which actually occurred
b_rows_sample.statement: States that chronology determines which of two different intellectual histories occurred (technical discovery preceding philosophical recognition, or vice versa) and that only the actual Evidence Ledger -- not narrative preference -- can establish which; reframes Step 215's most important task as determining 'when did the idea enter the reasoning', not merely what was concluded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 182 Steps -> 43 SignificantEvents -> 17 CoreInsights -> 8 ArchitecturalPrinciples -> 4 MajorThemes. The exact numbers are unknown
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a compression pipeline reducing 182 raw steps to a small number of significant events, core insights, architectural principles, and major themes (illustrative counts only, explicitly not fixed), arguing the book should present the intellectual structure hidden inside the steps rather than the 182 steps themselves; proposes an intermediate 5-epoch structure (Problem Recognition -> Experimentation -> DDD/Domain Modeling -> Mathematical/Epistemic Formalization -> KnowledgeOS/AI-Engineering Architecture) explicitly not to be frozen before the evidence determines it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture_observed ... Architecture_designed ... Architecture_implemented ... Architecture_proposed ... Observed ≠ Intended ≠ Implemented ≠ Target
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that the single word 'architecture' conflates at least four distinct referents (observed, intended, implemented, target/proposed) that may differ from each other, proposing Observed!=Intended!=Implemented!=Target as a central reconstruction rule; separately notes that linguistic markers in generated text ('should' signals P, 'the code contains' signals F if verified, 'therefore requires' signals D) can help automatically classify epistemic status at scale.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step Source Artifact Date/Sequence Primary Topic Type Observation Fact Hypothesis Experiment Result Derived Insight Decision Rejected Alternative Architectural Principle Invariant Evidence Gita Connection Status [F/D/P/U] Confidence Open Question
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the Step 215 Artifact: a 19-column Master Reconstruction Matrix schema intended as the master source for eventual book-writing, including a dedicated 'Gita Connection' column and 'Rejected Alternative' column.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not: rewrite the book; freeze the chapter structure; invent missing evidence; merge competing concepts; eliminate contradictions; assume implementation ... Reconstruct. Analyze. Synthesize. Write.
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists nine things not to do before reconstruction is complete (rewrite the book, freeze chapter structure, invent missing evidence, merge competing concepts, eliminate contradictions, assume implementation, over-architect philosophical analogies, assign arbitrary percentages, create formulas for their own sake), sequencing the correct order as Reconstruct -> Analyze -> Synthesize -> Write.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Phase 1 — Archaeology ... Phase 2 — Separation of Concerns ... Phase 3 — Synthesis ... This is the correct point at which Claude should eventually begin chapter-by-chapter writing. Not before
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a three-phase book-production architecture: Phase 1 Archaeology (S1..S182 -> Evidence Ledger, understand what happened), Phase 2 Separation of Concerns (separate Facts from Derivations from Proposals from PhilosophicalInterpretations, preventing conceptual contamination), Phase 3 Synthesis (Evidence->Patterns->Principles->Architecture->Book), stating chapter-by-chapter writing is correct only after all three phases, not before.

b_rows_sample.anchor: B = Synthesize(Evidence,Experiments,Failures,Insights,Architecture,PhilosophicalReflection) ... ClaimStrength ≤ EvidenceStrength ... PhilosophicalReflection ≠ TechnicalEvidence ... CurrentArchitecture ≠ TargetArchitecture
b_rows_sample.statement: States the final synthesis equation for the whole book-generation process, B=Synthesize(Evidence,Experiments,Failures,Insights,Architecture,PhilosophicalReflection), subject to three boxed constraints (ClaimStrength<=EvidenceStrength, PhilosophicalReflection!=TechnicalEvidence, CurrentArchitecture!=TargetArchitecture), explicitly framed as protecting the book against retrospective rewriting, overclaiming, and confusing philosophy with engineering proof.

b_rows_sample.anchor: It should be the actual execution of the reconstruction ... I should not fabricate their contents from the current conversation ... Once they are available here, we can process them in batches
b_rows_sample.statement: Previews Step 216: not another theoretical step but the actual execution of the reconstruction, explicitly refusing to fabricate the contents of Steps 1-182 from memory/conversation and requiring the real historical artifacts to be brought in and processed in batches, after which Step 183 onward may need renaming or absorption into the synthesis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: MATCH VERDICT: 6 of 8 agenda items delivered; 2 named and NOT delivered
a_rows_sample.statement: Probe (a): Step 207's tail agenda for Step 208 lists eight items (contract composition, information preservation, semantic loss, version compatibility, monotonicity, contradiction, uncertainty propagation, provenance preservation) under the question 'can a chain of individually valid transformations produce an invalid or misleading conclusion?'. Step 208 delivers 6 of 8: version compatibility is NOT delivered (Version appears only as a tuple field; no compatibility relation between contract versions is defined) and uncertainty propagation is NOT delivered (Section 208.14 shows uncertainty being lost, but no composition rule for uncertainty through C_2 o C_1 is given, and the word 'propagation' never occurs in Step 208). Additionally the headline question is restated, not quoted: 207 asks about an 'invalid or misleading conclusion'; 208 asks only whether the chain is 'necessarily valid' -- 'misleading' is dropped entirely and never addressed as distinct from invalidity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 208 neither cites nor consumes Step 82 (Uncertainty Propagation)
a_rows_sample.statement: The corpus already contains a dedicated prior step, '# Step 82 — Uncertainty Propagation', whose own Section 1 states 'we now test whether our mathematical model remains correct when uncertainty passes through multiple layers' -- exactly the agenda item Step 207 assigned to Step 208. Step 208 both omits the item (uncertainty propagation) and omits the prior work that already addressed it, with zero citation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Answered from scratch: zero citations to Steps 048/050/058
a_rows_sample.statement: Probe (b): machine grep of Step 208 (and all 8 in-scope files) for the prior corpus's answers to the same headline question -- Step 048's boxed 'LocalCorrectness ⇏ GlobalCorrectness', Step 058's boxed 'CorrectContexts ⇏ CorrectComposition', and Step 050's Attack 5 ('semantic collision', PASS) -- finds zero matches anywhere in the band. Step 208 Section 208.13 re-derives the same proposition in new notation ('locally valid but globally invalid'), so the same proposition is now boxed four times in the corpus in four notations with zero cross-reference; under LATER != SUPERSEDING, Step 208 does not supersede 048 or 058, it duplicates them without knowing they exist. Step 208's Section 208.22 (contradiction propagation) and Section 208.15 (RichEvidence -> SimpleBoolean) likewise re-derive the ground of Step 050's Attack 2 and Attack 5 respectively, also uncited.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Further arithmetic checks: 0.87>=0.80 correct; 0.91+/-0.08 within range at 1 sigma but 2-sigma bound exceeds 1; ratio checks disclaimed
a_rows_sample.statement: Additional independently-verified arithmetic in the band: Step 209 Section 209.15's 0.87 >= 0.80 evaluates to True (correct). Step 208 Section 208.14 / Step 210 Section 210.12's 0.91 +/- 0.08 gives [0.83, 0.99], within [0,1] at 1-sigma, but at 2-sigma the upper bound is 1.07 > 1 -- out of range for a quantity called 'confidence', though the corpus never commits this specific error since the interval's coverage level is left unlabelled. Step 215 Section 215.24's ratios (182/43=4.233, 43/17=2.529, 17/8=2.125, 8/4=2.0, total 45.5x) make no arithmetic claim and are correctly disclaimed as unknown. Step 209 Section 209.42 vs Step 210 Section 210.25: |I_KOS|=8 vs |{I1..I15}|=15, difference 7, mapping absent (unreconciled).

a_rows_sample.anchor: FORMAL OBJECTS: C_chain=C_3∘C_2∘C_1; Semantic Sufficiency S_B⊆I(C(A)); L(C)=I_required-I_preserved; SI(C,B)=True; Booleanization; KnowledgeArtifact 6-tuple
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 ('Semantic Contract Algebra') treats a DDD context contract as an information-preserving projection and defines: semantic sufficiency S_B ⊆ I(C(A)) relative to a receiving context's task; minimal sufficient contract; semantic projection pi; semantic loss L(C) = I_required - I_preserved; semantic integrity SI(C,B); the anti-pattern 'Booleanization' (collapsing rich epistemic state into a Boolean); contract temporal validity C(t); provenance composition P(G)=P(A)∪P(E); the KnowledgeArtifact 6-tuple (Content, Meaning, Provenance, Validity, Version, EpistemicStatus); the Data->Information->Evidence->Assessment->KnowledgeClaim ladder; Proposition as a first-class object; and a four-layer architecture split (Epistemic/Normative/Decisional/Operational).

a_rows_sample.anchor: PREVIOUS DEPENDENCY (cited BY NUMBER). 1 — We continue from Step 207.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 cites exactly one prior step by number (Step 207, 'we continue from...') and nothing else -- not Steps 048, 058, 050, or 082. Later response in scope: Step 208's SI non-compositionality (Section 208.12) is restated in Step 211 Section 211.5 as 'Component correctness ⇏ System correctness'; Step 208's L(C) (Section 208.10) reappears in Step 212 Section 212.19 as L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) without Step 208's own caveat; Step 208's Section 208.14 example reappears in substance, uncredited, in Step 212 Section 212.20.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EVOLUTION VERDICT: PARTIALLY_RESOLVES / REVIVES; DEFINITION VERDICT: PARTIALLY_CLEAR
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 resolves 6 of 8 of Step 207's agenda items and, unknowingly, revives already-boxed results from Steps 048 and 058. Definitionally: Booleanization, Suff(C,B,Task), semantic projection, and the four-layer split are CLEAR. The information measure I(.) is NOT DEFINED -- Section 208.3 writes an ordinal comparison I(A)<I(E) and Section 208.10 writes a difference L(C)=I_required-I_preserved while itself stating 'we should not treat this as a literal numeric quantity until we define an information measure' -- the measure is never defined and the operations are performed anyway. S_B ('the information necessary to perform its legitimate responsibility') is AMBIGUOUS because 'legitimate' is never defined, so S_B cannot be constructed for any concrete B.

a_rows_sample.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 208.3 (compounded at 208.10); SECOND DEFECT: Section 208.25's provenance equation
a_rows_sample.statement: DERIVATION VERDICT PARTIALLY_VALID. I(A)<I(E) presupposes a total order on information content; I_required-I_preserved presupposes an interval scale; neither is established (Section 208.10 explicitly declines to establish one, then uses the operations anyway) -- every downstream claim quantifying loss is conditional on repairing this. Second defect: P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation,' is either vacuous (if closure holds, P(A)∪P(E)=P(A)) or self-refuting (if it does not, provenance is not closed); it also excludes any provenance contributed by the governance act itself, directly conflicting with Step 209 Section 209.4's Final(D) ⇒ DecisionBasis(D) ∧ Authority(D) (see Contradiction #2).

a_rows_sample.anchor: COMPUTABILITY: nothing in Step 208 reaches CONSTRUCTIBLE; TEST VERDICT: NOT_EXECUTED
a_rows_sample.statement: Computability ladder for Step 208's objects: Booleanization is DEFINED; Semantic Sufficiency S_B⊆I(C(A)) is DEFINED but not INPUTS_KNOWN (both S_B and I uninstantiated); L(C) is DEFINED but explicitly barred from COMPUTABLE by its own Section 208.10; the Contract Safety theorem (Section 208.37) is DEFINED but not DERIVED. Nothing in the file reaches CONSTRUCTIBLE. Test verdict NOT_EXECUTED (0 tests specified, 0 run); the nine review questions in Section 208.38 are a checklist, not tests.

a_rows_sample.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: STRONG on framing, WEAK on inference; MEASUREMENT VERDICT: FAILS on the information measure
a_rows_sample.statement: Statistically, Section 208.6's sufficient-statistic analogy is immediately and correctly fenced ('this is an analogy, not a claim that DDD contracts are literally sufficient statistics') but left un-cashed (no Fisher-Neyman factorization or formal criterion transposed), and Section 208.23's handling of conflicting estimates is sound but uncited against prior statistical steps (025N, 082). Measurement-wise: I(.) has no declared scale type yet is compared (<) and subtracted (-) -- arithmetic NOT justified; result=0.91 in one block silently becomes confidence=0.91 in the very next (unjustified type conversion between a point estimate and a degree of belief); uncertainty=0.08 is silently converted into a symmetric +/-0.08 interval half-width in Step 210 Section 210.12, presupposing an unstated symmetric error distribution and coverage level; epistemic strength S(x) is compared with > (Section 208.9 forward) while Step 209 Section 209.21 later explicitly retracts any universal total ordering on the same kind of quantity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD VERDICT: STRONG — the best DDD content in the band; UBIQUITOUS-LANGUAGE: Evidence != Claim boxed, then violated two files later
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208's sufficiency-relative-to-responsibility (Section 208.4) is a correct, non-obvious Published-Language/conformist-boundary formulation; S_B ⊆ I(C(A)) ≪ I(A) (Section 208.5) is precisely the anti-Shared-Kernel constraint; Booleanization (Section 208.16) is a genuinely useful named anti-pattern; the four-layer split (Section 208.36) is a defensible strategic decomposition -- but none of it is mapped to Step 206's bounded contexts or Step 207's actual context contracts. Section 208.28 rules 'we should not collapse [Data/Information/Evidence/Assessment/KnowledgeClaim] into one generic object called Knowledge' -- a ruling violated two files later (Contradiction #1). Section 208.30 promotes Proposition to a first-class term; Section 208.29 boxes Evidence != Claim but gives it no owning context ('term without an owner').

a_rows_sample.anchor: ASSUMPTIONS / HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS; UNDEFINED SYMBOLS in Step 208
a_rows_sample.statement: Stated assumptions: a contract is total and deterministic; information is set-like so subset applies; S_B is knowable a priori. Hidden assumptions: that an information measure exists at all (Section 208.10 defers it and nothing in the band supplies one); that provenance sets are finite and mergeable (required by P(A)∪P(E), never stated); that Valid(C) (Section 208.2) and SI(C,B) (Section 208.12) are different predicates, though the text slides between them; that 'legitimate responsibility' (Section 208.4) is externally given, smuggling the governance model into the definition of sufficiency. Undefined symbols: I(.) (deferred), S_B (depends on undefined 'legitimate'), T_1, A_I/G_I/D_I, Preserve(.), RequiredProvenance(R_C), Knowledge(E).

a_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT SURVIVES / WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE — Step 208
a_rows_sample.statement: Survives: Booleanization as a named anti-pattern; Suff(C,B,Task) (purpose-relative sufficiency); the four-layer split; Evidence != Claim; probability-of-proposition != truth-value-of-proposition; the explicit refusal to claim contracts are sufficient statistics; non-monotonicity as a requirement; the boxed claim 'the objective is not zero information loss, the objective is zero loss of relevant meaning' (the band's clearest and most durable architectural statement). Does not survive: L(C) as any quantity; I(A)<I(E) as a comparison; P(G)=P(A)∪P(E); the Section 208.37 'provisional architectural theorem' (Sufficiency+Provenance+Temporal Validity ⇒ Contract Safety), which is a definition dressed as an implication since Contract Safety is not independently defined -- not a theorem in any sense, a naming convention.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The symbol I is silently rebound between Step 208 (information measure) and Step 209 onward (invariant) with no announcement
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 uses I exclusively for an information measure (I(E), I(A), I_required, I_preserved); Step 209 onward uses I exclusively for invariants (I_L, I_C, I_S, I_i, I_identity, I1-I15, I(s)). The rebinding is never announced -- a reader comparing I(C(A)) (Section 208.4, information) to I(s)=True (Section 210.32, an invariant predicate) is reading two different symbols under one glyph.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A and Gap: eight bindings of A, four bindings of Gap with two different ordinal category sets
a_rows_sample.statement: A denotes: Assessment (208-212, throughout), an aggregate state A_t (209.13), the architecture-as-CSP set A (209.34), an assurance vector (211.9), an AI-artifact 7-tuple (211.21), a statistical-result 8-tuple (210.13), an architecture snapshot A_t (213.16-18), and an artifact A_j (213.4) -- eight bindings, with Section 209.13's aggregate-state A_t formally indistinguishable in notation from Section 213.17-18's architecture-state A_t (delta(A_t,c)=A_{t+1} vs A_0->A_1->...). Gap denotes: a numeric difference (211.4, 212.10), an ordinal category (211.4's {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} vs 212.10's different {None,Partial,Significant,Critical,Unknown}), a class (212.11 G1-G5), and a register row (212.31 G-01-G-15) -- four bindings, with the two ordinal category sets differing from each other.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #1 — Knowledge as a generic object: forbidden in 208, used as an Owner in 210
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.28 boxes a prohibition: the Data->Information->Evidence->Assessment->KnowledgeClaim transformations of semantic status 'should not [be collapsed] into one generic object called Knowledge.' Step 210 Section 210.25's matrix row I11 nonetheless assigns Owner='Knowledge' (and row I3 compounds it with 'Knowledge infrastructure'), the exact generic object Step 208 boxed a prohibition against two files earlier in the same band. Severity HIGH; neither Step-206 bounded context, and neither file notices.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #14 — Subtraction on an undefined information measure, forbidden in Step 208 and performed anyway in Step 212
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.10 writes L(C)=I_required-I_preserved and immediately cautions 'we should not treat this as a literal numeric quantity until we define an information measure.' Step 212 Section 212.19 writes L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) without that caveat and without citing 208.10 -- no information measure is defined anywhere in the intervening four files. This is the fourth occurrence of the pattern in the band (208.3's I(A)<I(E), 208.10, 212.19, and 214.7's SemanticLoss(A)>0). Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 208 load-bearing boxed claims: Semantic Sufficiency, the provisional Contract-Safety theorem, and the survivor 'zero loss of relevant meaning'
a_rows_sample.statement: Three load-bearing boxed claims of Step 208, adjudicated: (1) 'Semantic Sufficiency: S_B⊆I(C(A))' -- the file's central definition, resting on the undefined I(.) and the undefined 'legitimate responsibility' in S_B. (2) 'Semantic Sufficiency + Provenance Preservation + Temporal Validity ⇒ Contract Safety' -- self-labelled 'a provisional architectural theorem, not a mathematically proven theorem'; verifier judges it a stipulative definition of Contract Safety rather than an implication, since the consequent is not independently defined. (3) 'The objective is not zero information loss. The objective is zero loss of relevant meaning.' -- survives; the band's clearest and most durable architectural statement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: each file's tail contains the agenda for the next step
b_rows_sample.statement: Structural observation, load-bearing for the whole verification: each file in the 208-215 band ends with the agenda section for the *next* step (e.g. the file titled 'Step 208' ends with a '# Step 209' section at line 1423 onward), so the band is a chain of overlapping documents and every 'Step N' agenda exists in two places (as the prior file's tail and the next file's own opening).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Prior-family acknowledgement in Step 209: NONE. ZERO.
b_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-i): machine grep of Step 209 for the corpus's prior invariant-naming families (INV-n, AFR-0n, GT-0n, GG-/GE-/GC-/GA-, IR-0n, CM-0n, LA-0n, AAI, PLP, and bare C1-C7/S1-S6/K1-K7/V1-V10/I1-I20) finds zero matches of any kind; Step 209 cites exactly one prior step (Step 208, in its opening line) and nothing else. The prior families are independently confirmed present and locatable in the corpus (AFR-0* in 3 files, INV-1* in 1, GT-0* in 1, AAI in 2, PLP in 1, IR-0* in 1, CM-0* in 1, LA-0* in 1); none is reconciled, mapped, superseded, or mentioned. Also uncited: Step 048 (global invariants), Step 092 (invariant preservation), Step 025N (a prior 'algebra' -- Evidence Aggregation Algebra), Step 091 (safety/liveness ground for Step 209's own Sections 209.35-37).

b_rows_sample.anchor: IS IT AN ALGEBRA? NO.
b_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-ii): an algebra requires a carrier set, closed operations, and laws. Step 209 supplies none of the three properly: the carrier ('an invariant') is never typed and is used interchangeably as a predicate on states (I(s)), a proposition (I_1 ∧ I_2), and a named object (I_identity) within one file; the only operation is unqualified conjunction (I_global = AND of I_i), imported from propositional logic and never defined on the carrier; no laws are stated (no associativity, commutativity, identity element, closure, absorption, or distributivity). The only other algebraic-looking object, A = {C,I,S,T,R} (Section 209.34), is ill-typed: written in set-brace notation for what the surrounding text treats as an ordered heterogeneous 5-tuple, so it cannot support the componentwise access the text assumes. Verdict: Step 209 is a taxonomy plus a conjunction, mislabelled an algebra -- a useful, well-organised three-level taxonomy of invariants (local/context/system), not an algebra.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Satisfiability is declared and never tested
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.32 declares that I_global = AND(I_1..I_n) 'is only valid if the invariants are jointly satisfiable' and states SAT(I_1 ∧ I_2 ∧ ... ∧ I_n) 'is an important next mathematical direction' but never tests it: COMPUTABILITY verdict DEFINED, not CONSTRUCTIBLE (the I_i are natural-language predicates, not formulas in any decidable logic), not COMPUTED, not TESTED. Section 209.33 constructs a hypothetical unsatisfiable pair (Action->Approval vs Action->ImmediateExecution) and does not check it against the actual I_KOS set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Cardinality drift: the 8-set I_KOS is silently superseded by a 15-list I1-I15 without amendment
b_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-iii): Step 209 Section 209.42 boxes and freezes an 8-member invariant set I_KOS = {I_identity, I_version, I_provenance, I_temporal, I_epistemic, I_authority, I_decision, I_execution}. Step 210 Section 210.25 then tabulates 15 invariants I1-I15 with no mapping given between the 8 and the 15. Independently checked: I13 (illegal transitions rejected) and I14 (preconditions/postconditions) have no member of I_KOS to belong to, and I15 (no semantic strengthening) is likewise unhoused unless forced into I_epistemic. The 8-set is silently superseded by the 15-list without amendment; only Step 209's own caveat ('we should not freeze this yet') prevents this from being an outright contradiction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Further arithmetic checks: 0.87>=0.80 correct; 0.91+/-0.08 within range at 1 sigma but 2-sigma bound exceeds 1; ratio checks disclaimed
b_rows_sample.statement: Additional independently-verified arithmetic in the band: Step 209 Section 209.15's 0.87 >= 0.80 evaluates to True (correct). Step 208 Section 208.14 / Step 210 Section 210.12's 0.91 +/- 0.08 gives [0.83, 0.99], within [0,1] at 1-sigma, but at 2-sigma the upper bound is 1.07 > 1 -- out of range for a quantity called 'confidence', though the corpus never commits this specific error since the interval's coverage level is left unlabelled. Step 215 Section 215.24's ratios (182/43=4.233, 43/17=2.529, 17/8=2.125, 8/4=2.0, total 45.5x) make no arithmetic claim and are correctly disclaimed as unknown. Step 209 Section 209.42 vs Step 210 Section 210.25: |I_KOS|=8 vs |{I1..I15}|=15, difference 7, mapping absent (unreconciled).

b_rows_sample.anchor: FORMAL OBJECTS: I_L(A), I_C(BC), I_S(System); Execution cannot manufacture authority; Semantic Laundering; I_KOS 8-set
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 ('Invariant Algebra') stratifies invariants into local/context/system levels (I_L, I_C, I_S); defines Verified(E)⇒Provenance(E)∧Integrity(E), Valid(A)⇒EvidenceBasis(A)∧ModelVersion(A), Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D), Executed(X)⇒Authorized(X) boxed as 'Execution cannot manufacture authority'; an epistemic partial order and knowledge lattice; 'Semantic Laundering' (a downstream context losing provenance/uncertainty of an upstream claim and treating the result as stronger than warranted); 'Determinism != Correctness'; architecture-as-CSP A={C,I,S,T,R}; safety properties P1-P4 and liveness properties L1-L2; and the boxed 8-member frozen set I_KOS={I_identity,I_version,I_provenance,I_temporal,I_epistemic,I_authority,I_decision,I_execution}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PREVIOUS DEPENDENCY: 1 (Step 208 only); LATER RESPONSE: Step 210 replaces I_KOS with I1-I15 without amendment
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 cites exactly one prior step (Step 208) and zero prior invariant families. Later response in scope: Step 210 Section 210.25 replaces the 8-member I_KOS with a 15-row I1-I15 without amendment; Step 210 Section 210.9 restates Step 209's Section 209.25 semantic-strength principle as Strength(T(x))>Strength(x) requires Justified(T); Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints I1-I15.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVOLUTION VERDICT: REFRAMES; DEFINITION VERDICT: PARTIALLY_CLEAR with one ILL-TYPED object
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 reframes scattered '!=' observations into a stratified system but does not resolve the SAT question it raises nor reconcile with any prior invariant family. CLEAR: the three-level stratification, Executed(X)⇒Authorized(X), semantic laundering, determinism!=correctness. ILL-TYPED: A={C,I,S,T,R} uses set-brace notation for an ordered heterogeneous 5-tuple, which has no positional structure though the surrounding text requires componentwise access. NOT_DEFINED: the type of 'an invariant' itself, used as a predicate on states, a proposition, and a named object within one file. INCOMPLETE: I_KOS's eight members are one-word labels with no formulas, unlike the file's own worked examples.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 209.32 (conjunction written as established, satisfiability tested after, never run)
b_rows_sample.statement: I_global = AND_{i=1}^n I_i (Section 209.32) is written as an established equality, and the satisfiability precondition (SAT test) is stated only afterward, as future work, never run. If the I_i are not jointly satisfiable then I_global is identically false and the boxed I_global = AND(I_KOS) is an assertion of contradiction. Everything downstream that treats I_global as a satisfiable target -- Step 210's matrix, Step 211's AAG, Step 212's gap register -- is conditional on repairing this. Secondary: Section 209.14's determinism claim (SameState+SameCommand⇒SameDomainResult) is used inconsistently as assumption, requirement, and derived property without saying which.

b_rows_sample.anchor: COMPUTABILITY: nothing reaches CONSTRUCTIBLE; TEST VERDICT: NOT_EXECUTED
b_rows_sample.statement: I_L/I_C/I_S stratification is DEFINED; I_KOS's 8 members are DEFINED but not INPUTS_KNOWN (unformalized); SAT(I_1∧...∧I_n) and SAT(A) are DEFINED but not CONSTRUCTIBLE (natural-language predicates, no decidable-logic encoding, and A is ill-typed); P1-P4/L1-L2 are DEFINED, self-described as 'candidates, not yet final requirements'; delta(A_t,c), Pre, Post are DEFINED with no aggregate instantiated. The file's own Section 209.34 concedes 'this is not yet a complete formal verification system.' Test verdict NOT_EXECUTED -- P1-P4 are called 'excellent candidates for deterministic assurance tests', none written or run.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: STRONG; MEASUREMENT VERDICT: MIXED with a good refusal and a violation
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209's separation of probabilistic inference from deterministic governance (Section 209.15), Determinism!=Correctness (Section 209.16), InvalidModelApplication!=LowConfidence (Section 209.17, a genuinely important distinction between model misspecification and wide posteriors), HighUncertainty!=KnownIncorrect / LowUncertainty!=GuaranteedTrue (Section 209.18), and ObservedCorrelation⇏Causation (Section 209.29, uncited against Step 074) are all statistically correct. Measurement: Section 209.21 correctly declines to universalize a total order on epistemic strength (Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported, 'should not be interpreted as a universal total ordering') -- a good refusal -- but Section 209.25 then writes S(T(x))>S(x), a strict comparison requiring exactly the order just declined, four pages later with no reconciliation. KnowledgeState=(EvidenceStrength,Consistency,Uncertainty) is correctly presented as a partial order/lattice admitting incomparable elements, with no arithmetic attempted (correct). I_global=AND(I_KOS) conjoins a nominal set of one-word labels that are not propositions -- a type gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DDD VERDICT: STRONG on structure, WEAK on consistency boundaries; UL: 'Semantic Laundering' the best-defined new term
b_rows_sample.statement: The I_L/I_C/I_S stratification is textbook-correct and the clearest statement of the aggregate/context/system-invariant distinction in the corpus; Section 209.6 correctly identifies Decision.AssessmentRef⇒Resolvable(AssessmentRef) as crossing aggregates, but DDD's standard remedy (a consistency-boundary decision -- strong vs eventual consistency, process manager/saga) is never offered, despite the corpus already containing '# Step 166 — Process Managers, Sagas' (uncited). 'Semantic Laundering' (Section 209.24: 'a downstream context loses the provenance or uncertainty of an upstream claim and treats the transformed result as stronger than its source warrants') is judged the single best-defined new term in the band; against this, I_KOS's eight members enter the language as labels without definitions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ASSUMPTIONS / HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS: conjunction cannot express the dependency graph the file itself draws
b_rows_sample.statement: Stated assumptions: invariants are propositions closed under AND; a single global conjunction is the right composition; governance transitions can be made deterministic. Hidden: that conjunction is the only composition operator needed, despite Section 209.31's dependency graph showing invariants depending on one another (a relation AND cannot express) -- Sections 209.31 and 209.32 are structurally inconsistent, a dependency graph is not a flat conjunction (Internal Contradiction #B); that the I_i are mutually independent, contradicted by 209.31; that I_KOS's eight members cover the space, with no completeness argument (Step 210 immediately produces 15). Undefined symbols: Integrity(E), EvidenceBasis(A), AssessmentMethod(A), DecisionBasis(D), ApplicablePolicy(D), Resolvable(.), Traceable(D,Basis(D)), Basis(D), S(x), EvidenceStrength/Consistency components, Eventually(.), and every member of I_KOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT SURVIVES / WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE — Step 209
b_rows_sample.statement: Survives: the three-level invariant stratification; Semantic Laundering; Determinism!=Correctness; InvalidModelApplication!=LowConfidence; Execution cannot manufacture authority; identity continuity independent of state continuity; the safety/liveness lens; the insight that a constitution should constrain invariants, not technologies. Does not survive: the title (it is not an algebra); A={C,I,S,T,R} as typed; SAT(A) as computable; I_global=AND(I_KOS) as a verified-satisfiable object (unverified, and structurally at odds with the dependency graph of Section 209.31); S(T(x))>S(x) as a well-formed comparison.

b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 uses I exclusively for an information measure (I(E), I(A), I_required, I_preserved); Step 209 onward uses I exclusively for invariants (I_L, I_C, I_S, I_i, I_identity, I1-I15, I(s)). The rebinding is never announced -- a reader comparing I(C(A)) (Section 208.4, information) to I(s)=True (Section 210.32, an invariant predicate) is reading two different symbols under one glyph.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Evidence/Test ordering is reversed between files, and Step 210's own boxed conclusion contradicts Step 210's own tuple
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209's tail agenda for 210 orders Invariant->Owner->EnforcementPoint->Test->Evidence->FailureMode; Step 210's own Section 210.1 tuple orders enforcement, monitoring, test, failure (test before the implied evidence); but Step 210's own boxed Section 210.40 conclusion states Invariant->Owner->Enforcement->Evidence->Test->Assurance (evidence before test); Step 211 Section 211.2 (boxed) and Step 214 Section 214.2 (boxed) both revert to Test before Evidence. Four sources agree that Test precedes Evidence; Step 210's one boxed conclusion disagrees with all of them, including with its own tuple -- the direction matters (Evidence->Test means evidence licenses the test; Test->Evidence means the test produces the evidence, which is what Steps 212-214 assume throughout). This is Contradiction #5.

b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.21 states Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported and explicitly declines a universal total ordering ('the actual epistemic lattice must be derived from the domain'). Step 209 Section 209.25 (S(T(x))>S(x)) and Step 210 Section 210.9 (Strength(T(x))>Strength(x)) both then use strict > on the same kind of quantity, presupposing the order that was just declined four sections earlier and never derived. group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 8 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: F | D | P | U ... F = Fact ... D = Derived ... P = Proposed ... U = Unknown
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a four-way epistemic classification for every architectural statement: F=Fact (directly supported by engineering evidence), D=Derived (logically derived from facts/observations), P=Proposed (a recommendation or future design), U=Unknown (insufficient evidence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: We designed the system according to this architecture from the beginning ... That would be misleading. The intellectually stronger story is: Experience -> Problem -> Observation -> Experiment -> Pattern -> Abstraction -> Theory -> Architecture
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns against retrospectively rewriting the book's history as if the system had been designed according to the derived architecture from the beginning, calling this misleading; proposes instead the causal chain Experience->Problem->Observation->Experiment->Pattern->Abstraction->Theory->Architecture as the intellectually stronger and more honest narrative.

a_rows_sample.anchor: How can this artifact support our current theory? We should ask: What does this artifact actually establish?
a_rows_sample.statement: States the archaeological method's central mindset shift: treat prior artifacts (prompts, AI outputs, architecture docs, ADRs, code, tests, rejected ideas, contradictions, revisions) as evidence to be asked 'what does this actually establish', never 'how does this support our current theory'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: E(A_j)={Facts,Observations,Decisions,Assumptions,Experiments,Failures,Questions} ... Artifact -> Evidence -> Interpretation. Not: Theory -> selective evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines evidence extraction per artifact E(A_j) as the set {Facts,Observations,Decisions,Assumptions,Experiments,Failures,Questions}, to be connected to architectural concepts only afterward (Artifact->Evidence->Interpretation), explicitly rejecting the reverse flow Theory->selective evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance enforcement could not yet be established from the available evidence ... unless we have evidence of absence
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires that absence of knowledge about whether a property (e.g. provenance) exists in an implementation be written as Unknown ('could not yet be established from the available evidence'), never as an assertion of absence ('is missing') unless positive evidence of absence exists.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Prov(C)={A_1,A_2,...,A_n} ... provenance of architecture itself
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes giving architectural claims themselves a provenance set Prov(C)={A_1,...,A_n} of supporting artifacts, so a reader can trace Claim->Evidence -- termed 'provenance of architecture itself'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ADL = Decision -> Problem -> Evidence -> Alternatives -> Rationale -> Consequence
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an Architecture Decision Lineage ADL = Decision->Problem->Evidence->Alternatives->Rationale->Consequence, proposed to eventually become part of the KnowledgeOS architecture itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Failure -> Knowledge ... some of the strongest architectural principles may originate from failed approaches ... What did not work ... alongside ... What eventually worked. Otherwise the final architecture looks inevitable
a_rows_sample.statement: States the negative-result principle: a failed experiment (Hypothesis H tested, Result=not-H) is Failure->Knowledge, not useless, and some of the strongest architectural principles may originate from failed approaches; the book should explicitly record what did not work alongside what eventually worked, because otherwise the final architecture looks falsely inevitable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ChosenPattern ... RejectedPattern ... ReasonForRejection
a_rows_sample.statement: Connects the negative-result principle to the corpus's Chapter 4 theme: knowledge includes discrimination between Valid and Invalid, so the architecture should preserve not only the ChosenPattern but sometimes the RejectedPattern and ReasonForRejection.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A_{t+1}=E(A_t, Evidence_t) ... Architecture is not merely documentation growth. It is knowledge evolution
a_rows_sample.statement: Models architecture evolution as A_{t+1}=E(A_t,Evidence_t) driven by new evidence, explicitly rejecting the weaker model A_{t+1}=A_t+more documentation; calls architecture 'knowledge evolution', not documentation growth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ΔA=(Trigger,Evidence,Decision,Rationale,Impact)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an architecture-evolution tuple DeltaA=(Trigger,Evidence,Decision,Rationale,Impact) as the architecture's evolutionary provenance record for each change.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Stage 1 ... What problem was first recognized? ... Stage 7 What remains unverified?
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes reconstructing an 'epistemic chronology' (not necessarily calendar chronology) in seven stages: problem recognized, assumptions made, experiments challenging them, patterns emerged, abstractions introduced, resulting architecture, and what remains unverified -- proposed as the backbone of the eventual book.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observed Reality ... Architectural Interpretation ... Normative Design
a_rows_sample.statement: Separates three reconstruction layers: Observed Reality (what happened), Architectural Interpretation (what it means), and Normative Design (what should be built), illustrated with an AI-code-inconsistency example running observation->derived-knowledge->proposal.

a_rows_sample.anchor: O=observations ... D=g(O)=derived knowledge ... P=h(D)=proposed architecture ... P ⇏ O
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes O->D->P (observations, derived knowledge via D=g(O), proposed architecture via P=h(D)) with the explicit non-implication P does-not-imply O: a proposal cannot retroactively become evidence for the observation that motivated it, protecting the book from circular reasoning (e.g. avoiding 'we need deterministic assurance because KnowledgeOS is a deterministic assurance platform').

a_rows_sample.anchor: C_fact=High if directly supported by primary implementation evidence ... C_derived=Medium if the inference depends on assumptions ... avoid false numerical precision
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a qualitative confidence label (e.g. C_fact=High, C_derived=Medium) attached to F/D/P/U claims only when justified, again warning against false numerical precision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Primary ... source code; configuration; database schema; test result; runtime behavior; direct experiment ... Secondary ... AI analysis; architecture summary; meeting notes; retrospective explanation. Secondary evidence ... should not silently override primary evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Primary evidence (source code, configuration, database schema, test result, runtime behavior, direct experiment) from Secondary evidence (AI analysis, architecture summary, meeting notes, retrospective explanation), warning that secondary evidence must not silently override primary evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AIClaim -> Hypothesis. Then: ImplementationEvidence -> Fact ... AI Interpretation != Engineering Evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: States that an AI-generated statement (e.g. Claude or DeepSeek claiming 'the system uses invariant-driven architecture') is not itself proof but a hypothesis, only becoming Fact once corroborated by implementation evidence; boxes the AI epistemic boundary AI Interpretation != Engineering Evidence as one of the book's strongest intended methodological principles.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We are using AI to reconstruct an architecture for an AI engineering platform ... The architecture is therefore being used to validate the method by which it is being reconstructed ... The method is correct because it follows the architecture [is circular]
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes the self-referential situation of using AI to reconstruct the architecture of an AI engineering platform (a useful meta-level experiment), then explicitly warns against circular validation ('the method is correct because it follows the architecture'); the reconstruction method must independently satisfy Evidence+Reproducibility+Traceability before it can be said to exemplify the architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EAG=(Evidence,Claims,Decisions,Invariants,Architecture) ... Invariant -> Test -> Evidence. This creates a closed assurance loop
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Architecture Assurance Graph into an Evidence-Architecture-Graph EAG=(Evidence,Claims,Decisions,Invariants,Architecture) with edges Evidence->Claim->Decision->Architecture->Invariant and potentially Invariant->Test->Evidence, closing the assurance loop, then generalizes to the full cycle Observation->Knowledge->Architecture->Invariant->Implementation->Test->Evidence->NewKnowledge, calling architecture 'a learning system'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Learning -> ArchitectureDrift ... Architecture evolution must itself be governed
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns that ungoverned architectural learning becomes ArchitectureDrift, boxing the principle that architecture evolution must itself be governed, and lists six questions a software change should answer (what changed, why, which invariant is affected, which bounded context owns it, what evidence justifies it, how was it verified) as a stronger Software Change Governance model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We should not yet write another architectural theory step

a_rows_sample.statement: Systematically tests five candidate derivation routes into the operation set O / transformation set T from already-ratified material, finding all fail except direct declaration: deriving O from K is circular (K is downstream of minimality<-congruence<-T); deriving from the invariant universe is blocked since invariants are downstream of equiv (Step 287); deriving from a minimality proof fails since Step 259 states no valid minimality proof exists before transformation-congruence analysis; deriving from the ratified 8 primitives fails since those primitives have never been shown minimal against any operation space; enumerating the forced lower bound (256.2/259.7 give 14 forced operations, upper bound 18) yields only a candidate set, never a membership rule. a_rows_sample.anchor: F(do(a,s)) \equiv \gamma_F^+(a,s) \lor (F(s)\land\neg\gamma_F^-(a,s)) ... X_{t+1}=Add_X(e_t,K_t)\lor(X_t\land\neg Remove_X(e_t,K_t)) ... K_{t+1}=Apply(K_t,e_t,Add(e_t),Remove(e_t),Persist(e_t))
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines the delta candidate into a per-component successor-state decomposition: X_{t+1} = Add_X(e_t,K_t) OR (X_t AND NOT Remove_X(e_t,K_t)), generalized to K_{t+1}=Apply(K_t,e_t,Add,Remove,Persist); turns delta from an opaque 'something changes the state' into a testable structure asking what becomes true/false/persists, under which conditions, and what is unaffected. a_rows_sample.statement: AOL (Action + Only-Knowing Logic) integrates situation calculus (S0, do(a,s), fluents, successor-state axioms, Poss, sensing SF) with epistemic K(s,t)/Knows/OKnows-after-action definitions, giving a combined framework for how only-knowing evolves through actions and sensing -- a second, independent formal source (alongside Reiter directly) for the successor-state-semantics candidate, and the first source in this batch to combine Only-Knowing/Zero-style formalism with the dynamic/transition lane.

a_rows_sample.anchor: pickingUp(x,do(c,s))\equiv startPickup(x)\in c\lor(pickingUp(x,s)\land endPickup(x)\notin c) ... Poss(startMoveLeft,s)\equiv\neg movingLeft(s) ... Poss(\{startMoveLeft,startMoveRight\},s) should be false. The converse of the foundational axiom need not hold.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends successor-state semantics to concurrent action sets (successor-state axiom for a concurrent-action fluent), and identifies the 'precondition interaction problem': individually-possible concurrent actions (startMoveLeft, startMoveRight) can be jointly impossible even though each satisfies its own precondition axiom, requiring additional interaction constraints beyond the individual precondition axioms.

a_rows_sample.anchor: [EXT] throughout. Extracted, not endorsed. ... The induction axiom is second-order. The extraction states the consequence plainly: the system is not fully first-order decidable. Any transfer inherits this. ... It rests on the causal completeness assumption ... This is an assumption about the axiomatiser's knowledge, not a theorem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates Reiter's formal ontology and axioms (already captured in S2536) under an explicit [EXT]/'extracted not endorsed' framing, emphasizing two carried-forward limitations for any KnowledgeOS transfer: the induction axiom is second-order (not fully first-order decidable), and the successor-state axiom rests on an unproven causal-completeness ASSUMPTION about the axiomatiser's own knowledge, not a theorem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "conflicting_effects_from_F_false": ["F"], "conflicting_effects_from_F_true": ["F"], "conflict_resolved_silently_in_favour_of_gamma_plus": true, "finding": "when gamma+ and gamma- both name F, the SSA yields F TRUE with no signal that the effect axioms were inconsistent. The frame solution PRESUPPOSES consistent effect axioms; it does not detect their inconsistency."
a_rows_sample.statement: Executed result: a deliberately conflicting action (gamma+ and gamma- both naming fluent F) is silently resolved to F=TRUE from both prior states, with the successor-state axiom giving no signal that its own effect axioms were inconsistent -- confirming determinism and persistence-of-unmentioned-fluents work correctly, but exposing that inconsistency detection is entirely outside the mechanism's scope.

a_rows_sample.anchor: class Situation: """A situation IS a history: a finite sequence of actions.  NOT a state.""" ... def successor(self, a, state): """Successor state axiom:  F' = gamma+ ∨ (F ∧ ¬gamma-)""" ... def regress(self, fluent, sit): """REGRESSION: rewrite a query about sit into a query about S0, by unwinding the successor-state axiom backwards."""
a_rows_sample.statement: A minimal but faithful executable model of Reiter's situation calculus: a Situation as an immutable action tuple (explicitly a history, not a state), an ActionTheory with Poss/successor(SSA)/progress/executable/regress methods, used to generate all five A1-A5 experimental results in this batch; module docstring explicitly frames these as verification tests of Reiter's machinery, not a KnowledgeOS implementation, and states nothing here promotes any Reiter concept to a KnowledgeOS primitive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: TELL does not mean TELL \Rightarrow Truth ... ASK=TRUE does not automatically mean Truth
b_rows_sample.statement: TELL(K,alpha)->K' and ASK(K,r,Gamma)->Eval_c are candidate fundamental operations, grounded in the classical KR&R TELL/ASK pattern (systems that can be told facts and adjust behaviour); explicit KnowledgeOS restriction: TELL does not imply Truth (only that content entered the governed representation per applicable authority/admission rules), and ASK=TRUE does not automatically mean Truth (only that the applicable evaluation semantics returned that result).

b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends Levesque & Lakemeyer's Logic of Knowledge Bases as second priority, proposing its TELL/ASK interface (with the unhedged three-valued ASK return type later replaced by Eval_c in S2520/S2521) and its 'Only-Knowing' formal logic for 'all I know' as directly relevant to the open Zero TODO and the Closed-World-Assumption question.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ASK[alpha,e] = YES if e|=Kalpha; NO otherwise ... TELL[alpha,e]=e \cap \{w\mid e,w\models\alpha\} ... e,w\models K\alpha \iff for every w'\in e, e,w'\models\alpha
b_rows_sample.statement: Formal semantics for ASK[alpha,e] (YES iff e|=K-alpha, else NO) and TELL[alpha,e] (intersect e with the worlds satisfying alpha), and the K operator (K-alpha true at w iff alpha holds in every world w' in the epistemic state e) -- the precise formal machinery underlying the TELL/ASK candidate used loosely elsewhere in this batch.

b_rows_sample.anchor: (\alpha\supset K\alpha) FALSE ... (K\alpha\supset\alpha) FALSE ... If \models\alpha then \models K\alpha TRUE ... For any subjective sentence sigma: \models(\sigma\supset K\sigma) [positive introspection] ... logical omniscience
b_rows_sample.statement: Catalogues formal properties of K: truth does not imply knownness and knowledge need not be accurate (K models belief, not factive knowledge, in this framework) while valid sentences are always known; complete positive introspection holds for subjective sentences; and the K operator suffers logical omniscience (knows all logical consequences of what it knows) -- a limitation later addressed by the B operator.
